definition_en: to go faster, or to make something go faster
core_image: 脚掌把油门稳稳踩下去，窗外的树影连成一片
scene: 司机看到绿灯后踩下踏板，车速一下子提了上去。The train accelerated smoothly as it left the station.
sceneCN: 这里 accelerate 是「加速」（第 1 个义项：速度变快），句意是列车离站时平稳加速。

pos.zh: 动词：加速；使加快；促进

derivatives.zh: 加 -ation 构成，义为「加速、加速度」

senses.title: To move faster
senses.titleCN: 加速：本身速度变快
senses.definition: to gain speed in motion
senses.definitionCN: 运动速度变快
senses.example: The bus accelerated as the road opened up.
senses.exampleCN: 路一开阔，公交车就加速了。
senses.why: Latin accelera contained celer, swift; speed is what the verb first names.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 accelera 内藏 celer「快速」，速度是这个动词最先命名的东西。

senses.title: To make something quicker
senses.titleCN: 使加快：推动别的事物变快
senses.definition: to raise the speed of something else
senses.definitionCN: 使另一事物的速度提高
senses.example: New machines accelerated the whole line.
senses.exampleCN: 新机器使整条生产线加快了。
senses.why: The -ate ending makes an action word, so the verb can act on an outside thing.
senses.whyCN: -ate 词尾使其成为动作词，因此可以作用于外部事物。

senses.title: To speed up a process
senses.titleCN: 促进：让过程提前到来
senses.definition: to cause an event to come sooner
senses.definitionCN: 使某事更早发生
senses.example: War accelerated the spread of the invention.
senses.exampleCN: 战争加速了这项发明的传播。
senses.why: Time is the object here: the change is not in metres per second but in months.
senses.whyCN: 这里的对象是时间：变化不在每秒多少米，而在多少个月。

senses.title: To grow at a rising rate
senses.titleCN: 增速：增长越来越快
senses.definition: to increase at an increasing rate
senses.definitionCN: 以递增的比率增长
senses.example: Costs accelerated in the final quarter.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一个季度成本增速变快。
senses.why: When the rate itself rises, the word moves from speed to the shape of a curve.
senses.whyCN: 当比率本身在上升时，这个词便从速度转向曲线的形状。

intro.en: Accelerate comes from Latin accelerare, to hasten, from ad- plus celer, swift.
intro.cn: accelerate 来自拉丁语 accelerare「使加快」，由 ad- 加 celer「快速」构成。

items.en: Celer meant swift, and it also survives in celerity.
items.cn: celer 意为「快速」，也留在 celerity 里。

items.en: Accelerare meant to bring speed, with ad- adding direction toward.
items.cn: accelerare 意为「把速度带来」，ad- 补充了朝向之意。

items.en: Scholars kept accelerated as a term of motion and hurried action.
items.cn: 学者们用 accelerare 记运动与匆忙的行动。

items.en: English took accelerate for raising speed in physics.
items.cn: 英语借 accelerate 表物理学上的提速。

items.en: Industry applied it to processes and growth as well.
items.cn: 工业界又把它用到流程与增长上。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the celer root or the -ate ending; the near-meaning group holds words of speed.
note.cn: 形近组共用 celer 词根或 -ate 词尾；近义组收表示加快的词。

entries.definition: The act or rate of speeding up.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「加速、加速度」。

entries.definition: The thing that speeds something up.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「加速器、油门」。

entries.definition: Swiftness of movement, rare and formal.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「迅速」，与 accelerate 同根。

entries.definition: The everyday phrase for making something faster.
entries.definitionCN: 短语，义为「加快」，最日常的说法。

entries.definition: To make something happen sooner, often about events.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「催促、加快」，多用于事件。

entries.definition: To become or make faster, a gentler word than accelerate.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「变快、使加快」，语气较柔。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the celer root, the pedal image and the business sense.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借 celer 词根、油门意象与商务用法。

normal.en: Celer means swift, so accelerate carries speed in its own root.
normal.cn: celer 意为快速，因此 accelerate 的词根里就带着速度。

normal.en: The pedal under your foot is the accelerator, the thing that makes you accelerate.
normal.cn: 脚下的踏板是 accelerator，正是让你加速的东西。

normal.en: Accelerate a process sounds like paying months in advance.
normal.cn: accelerate a process 听起来像把几个月提前付掉。

normal.en: Decelerate is the mirror word, the same root with a minus sign.
normal.cn: decelerate 是对照词，同一词根带一个减号。

normal.en: In physics the noun acceleration measures how fast the speed itself changes.
normal.cn: 物理里 acceleration 量的是速度本身变化多快。

abstract.en: Speed is one number; acceleration is the growth of that number.
abstract.cn: 速度是一个数，加速度是那个数的增长。

abstract.en: Anything hurried takes time from somewhere, which is why the verb reaches months as easily as metres.
abstract.cn: 凡被催促的事都要从别处借时间，所以这个词既能通向米，也能通向月。

abstract.en: A slope that steepens is the shape of the word: the change is in the changing.
abstract.cn: 越来越陡的坡就是这个词的形状：变化在于变化本身。

examples.en: The car accelerated quickly on the empty road.
examples.cn: 车在空旷的路上迅速加速。

examples.en: Cheap flights accelerated the growth of weekend travel.
examples.cn: 廉价航班加快了周末旅行的增长。

examples.en: Warm weather can accelerate the ripening of the fruit.
examples.cn: 温暖的天气会加速果实的成熟。

dict_mnemonic.text: ac-（向）+ celer（快）+ -ate（动词）= 朝快的方向去 → 加速

root: 拉丁语 celer（快速）+ ad-（朝向）+ -are（动词词尾）→ accelerare（使加快）；同族词有 acceleration、accelerator、celerity、decelerate。

sensesIntro.en: Accelerate moves a thing, a process or a rate toward greater speed, and the four senses separate those three objects.
sensesIntro.cn: accelerate 把事物、过程或比率推向更快的速度，四个义项分别对应这三类对象。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a foot pressing the pedal until the scenery blurs.
core.cn: 核心意象：脚踩下踏板，风景糊成一片。

branches.en: MOTION LINE: the vehicle itself goes faster.
branches.cn: 运动线：车辆本身变快。

branches.en: CAUSE LINE: something else is made faster.
branches.cn: 施动线：别的对象被加快。

branches.en: TIME LINE: an event arrives sooner.
branches.cn: 时间线：事件更早到来。

branches.en: CURVE LINE: the rate of growth rises.
branches.cn: 曲线线：增长率本身上升。

branches.en: CONTRAST: to slow down is decelerate, the same root reversed.
branches.cn: 对照线：放慢是 decelerate，同一词根反向。

intro.en: A Latin prefix of direction on a root meaning swift, closed by a verb ending.
intro.cn: 一个表方向的前缀加「快速」词根，以动词词尾收束。

latinIntro.en: Ad- plus celer gives accelerare, to hasten, the ancestor of the English verb.
latinIntro.cn: ad- 加 celer 得到 accelerare「使加快」，即英语动词的祖先。

items.example: It points the root toward the object.

items.exampleCN: 它也出现在 celerity 里。

definition_en: the way a group of people sound when they speak, or the stress put on a part of a word
core_image: 同一句问候，从两个人口里出来，调子各自拐向不同的方向
scene: 他一开口，我们就听出他不是本地人。The teacher put the accent on the second syllable.
sceneCN: 这里 accent 是「口音」（第 1 个义项：说话的地域腔调）；后半句则指重音。

pos.zh: 名词：口音；腔调；重音；强调
动词：重读；强调

senses.title: Way of sounding
senses.titleCN: 口音：一个群体的说话腔调
senses.definition: the sound pattern of speech in a place or group
senses.definitionCN: 某地或某群体的说话声调特征
senses.example: She still speaks with a northern accent.
senses.exampleCN: 她说话仍带着北方口音。
senses.why: The noun began with song: accentus was a tune added to speech.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词起于歌唱：accentus 是加在言语上的调子。

senses.title: Stress in a word
senses.titleCN: 重音：词里的着力处
senses.definition: the stronger force given to one syllable
senses.definitionCN: 某一个音节上用力更重
senses.example: Where does the accent fall in this word?
senses.exampleCN: 这个词的重音落在哪里？
senses.why: From tune came the rise of the voice, and then the stressed beat of a word.
senses.whyCN: 由调子而有了声音的起伏，进而指词里那一下重拍。

senses.title: Emphasis on a point
senses.titleCN: 强调：对某一点的着力
senses.definition: special attention given to an idea
senses.definitionCN: 对某个意思给予特别关注
senses.example: The report puts the accent on safety.
senses.exampleCN: 报告把重点放在安全上。
senses.why: Stress can leave the syllable and fall on an argument or a policy.
senses.whyCN: 重音可以离开音节，落到一个论点或一项政策上。

senses.title: A mark over a letter
senses.titleCN: 变音符号：字母上的标记
senses.definition: a written sign showing sound or stress
senses.definitionCN: 标示发音或重音的书面记号
senses.example: The word café carries an accent on the final letter.
senses.exampleCN: café 一词在末字母上带一个变音符号。
senses.why: Writing borrowed the tune as a small mark above the vowel.
senses.whyCN: 书写把这个调子借为元音上的一点小记号。

intro.en: Accent comes from Latin accentus, a song added to speech, from ad- plus cantus, singing.
intro.cn: accent 来自拉丁语 accentus「加在言语上的歌」，由 ad- 加 cantus「歌唱」构成。

items.en: Canere meant to sing, and it underlies chant and canticle.
items.cn: canere 意为「歌唱」，也是 chant 与 canticle 的底层词。

items.en: Accentus named a tone added to spoken words, a kind of musical stress.
items.cn: accentus 指加在口语词上的调子，是一种音乐性的着力。

items.en: Old French acent carried both the sound and the written mark.
items.cn: 古法语 acent 同时指声音与书面记号。

items.en: English used accent for stress in a word and for the sound of a region.
items.cn: 英语用 accent 指词的重音，也指地方腔调。

items.en: Modern usage extends the word to emphasis placed on any point.
items.cn: 现代用法把这个词延伸到对任何要点的强调。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -ent ending or the cant- root; the near-meaning group holds words of speech and stress.
note.cn: 形近组共用 -ent 词尾或 cant- 词根；近义组收表示口音与重音的词。

entries.definition: To stress or make more noticeable.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「强调、使突出」。

entries.definition: An upward climb; two letters differ, the meaning does not meet.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「上升、攀登」，拼写近而意义不同。

entries.definition: Agreement given to a proposal.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「同意」，与 accent 形近。

entries.definition: A whole variety of speech, larger than an accent.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「方言」，范围比口音大。

entries.definition: The way sounds are produced, without the regional tune.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「发音」，不含地域腔调。

entries.definition: The plain word for force on a syllable or a point.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「重音、压力」，最直白的对应词。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the singing root, the syllable stress and the little written mark.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借「歌唱」词根、音节重音与那点书写记号。

normal.en: Accent and chant share a singing root: speech with a tune on it.
normal.cn: accent 与 chant 共用歌唱词根：言语上加了调子。

normal.en: Put the accent on the second syllable is the standard classroom sentence.
normal.cn: 「Put the accent on the second syllable」是课堂上的标准例句。

normal.en: A foreign accent is the sound of one place meeting another.
normal.cn: foreign accent 是一个地方的声音遇上另一个地方。

normal.en: Café keeps its accent mark so the last vowel still sings.
normal.cn: café 留着变音符号，让最后一个元音仍在唱。

normal.en: Accentuate the point, and the noun accent becomes a verb of emphasis.
normal.cn: accentuate the point，名词 accent 就变成了表强调的动词。

abstract.en: A tune borrowed from singing becomes a mark on paper, and the journey is the whole word.
abstract.cn: 从歌唱借来的调子变成纸上的记号，这段旅程就是这个词全部。

abstract.en: Every accent says where someone has been before they speak to you.
abstract.cn: 每种口音都在说你遇到他之前他去过哪里。

abstract.en: Stress moves from voice to syllable to argument, and the word goes with it.
abstract.cn: 着力从嗓音移到音节再移到论点，这个词也跟着移动。

examples.en: He speaks English with a slight French accent.
examples.cn: 他说英语带一点点法国口音。

examples.en: Put the accent on the first syllable in this noun.
examples.cn: 这个名词的重音放在第一个音节上。

examples.en: Her speech put the accent on what young workers need.
examples.cn: 她的演讲把重点放在年轻工人需要什么上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱磕声特」——爱磕某个声，那个声就特重，成了重音与口音

root: 拉丁语 cantus（歌唱）加 ad-（附加）→ accentus（加在言语上的调子）；同族词有 accentuate、chant、canticle、accentual。

sensesIntro.en: Accent runs from the tune of a voice to the stress inside a word, and then to stress placed on any idea.
sensesIntro.cn: accent 从嗓音的调子走到词内的重音，再走到加在任何想法上的着力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the same sentence rising differently in two mouths.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一句话在两个人口中起落不同。

branches.en: VOICE LINE: the sound of a region in the mouth.
branches.cn: 嗓音线：地域的声音落在口中。

branches.en: BEAT LINE: one syllable carries more force.
branches.cn: 节拍线：一个音节承受更多力。

branches.en: ARGUMENT LINE: attention given to one point.
branches.cn: 论点线：注意力给了一个要点。

branches.en: PAPER LINE: the tune shrinks to a written sign.
branches.cn: 纸面线：调子缩成一个书写记号。

branches.en: CONTRAST: a dialect is a whole system, an accent is its sound.
branches.cn: 对照线：方言是整套系统，口音是它的声音。

intro.en: A prefix of addition on a Latin root of singing.
intro.cn: 一个表附加的前缀加拉丁「歌唱」词根。

latinIntro.en: Ad- plus cantus, singing, gives accentus, a tone added to speech.
latinIntro.cn: ad- 加 cantus「歌唱」得到 accentus，即加在言语上的调子。

items.example: It adds the tune to the words.

items.exampleCN: 它也出现在 chant 里。

definition_en: to take something willingly that is offered, or to agree that something is true
core_image: 两只手伸出来，把递到面前的东西接住，没有推回去
scene: 他把简历又看了一遍，然后点头把职位接了下来。She accepted the gift with both hands.
sceneCN: 这里 accept 是「接受」（第 1 个义项：把递来的东西收下）；句意是她双手接过礼物。

pos.zh: 动词：接受；收下；承认；同意
不及物：接受；同意

derivatives.zh: 加 -ance 构成，义为「接受、接纳」

senses.title: To take what is offered
senses.titleCN: 接受：把递来的东西收下
senses.definition: to receive something offered without refusing it
senses.definitionCN: 不拒绝地收下别人递来的东西
senses.example: He accepted the cup of tea.
senses.exampleCN: 他接过了那杯茶。
senses.why: Latin accipere means to take to oneself; the hand closes on what arrives.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 accipere 意为「取到自己这里」，手在东西到来时合上。

senses.title: To agree to a proposal
senses.titleCN: 同意：应允一个提议
senses.definition: to say yes to an offer or invitation
senses.definitionCN: 对提议或邀请表示答应
senses.example: She accepted the job without hesitating.
senses.exampleCN: 她毫不犹豫地接受了这份工作。
senses.why: Taking becomes saying yes when the thing offered is not an object but an offer.
senses.whyCN: 当递来的不是物件而是提议时，收下便成了答应。

senses.title: To admit as true
senses.titleCN: 承认：认可某事为真
senses.definition: to agree that a fact or idea is true
senses.definitionCN: 同意某个事实或想法为真
senses.example: Most scientists accept the theory.
senses.exampleCN: 多数科学家接受这个理论。
senses.why: The mind can take a statement the way the hand takes a gift.
senses.whyCN: 头脑接过一句话，正如手接过一件礼物。

senses.title: To bear without protest
senses.titleCN: 承受：不抗拒地接受
senses.definition: to endure a hard situation calmly
senses.definitionCN: 平静地承受困难处境
senses.example: They accepted the loss and moved on.
senses.exampleCN: 他们接受了这次损失，继续往前走。
senses.why: What cannot be refused is still taken in, and the word turns quiet and heavy here.
senses.whyCN: 无法拒绝的东西仍被接进来，这个词在此变得安静而沉重。

intro.en: Accept comes from Latin accipere, to take to oneself, from ad- plus capere, to take.
intro.cn: accept 来自拉丁语 accipere「取到自己这里」，由 ad- 加 capere「拿取」构成。

items.en: Capere meant to take or seize, and it underlies capture and receive.
items.cn: capere 意为「拿取、抓住」，也是 capture 与 receive 的底层词。

items.en: Accipere meant to take something to oneself willingly.
items.cn: accipere 意为「自愿地把东西取到自己这边」。

items.en: Old French accepter carried the sense of receiving and approving.
items.cn: 古法语 accepter 带有「接收并认可」之意。

items.en: English accept meant to receive kindly and then to approve.
items.cn: 英语 accept 先指乐意接收，再指认可。

items.en: The word now covers gifts, offers, facts and hard outcomes.
items.cn: 这个词如今覆盖礼物、提议、事实与艰难的结果。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -cept root or the ac- prefix; the near-meaning group holds words of agreeing.
note.cn: 形近组共用 -cept 词根或 ac- 前缀；近义组收表示同意的词。

entries.definition: To leave one thing out; one letter changes the meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「除…之外」，与 accept 形极近。

entries.definition: The act of taking what is offered.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「接受、接纳」。

entries.definition: To take delivery of something, sharing the capere root.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「收到」，同 capere 词根。

entries.definition: To get something given or sent, whether you wished it or not.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「收到」，不论是否情愿。

entries.definition: The plain phrase for saying yes to a plan.
entries.definitionCN: 短语，义为「同意」，最日常的说法。

entries.definition: To admit a fact openly, close to the third sense.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「承认」，接近第三义项。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the take root, the open hand and the difference from except.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借「拿取」词根、张开的双手，以及与 except 的区别。

normal.en: Accept shares a root with capture: to take hold of what comes.
normal.cn: accept 与 capture 同根：把到来的东西握住。

normal.en: Accept has ac-, except has ex-, so one takes in and one leaves out.
normal.cn: accept 是 ac-，except 是 ex-，一个接进来，一个排除掉。

normal.en: Accept an offer is the everyday office phrase for saying yes.
normal.cn: accept an offer 是办公室里最常说的答应。

normal.en: Accept the fact sits halfway between agreeing and enduring.
normal.cn: accept the fact 介于认可与承受之间。

normal.en: Acceptance is the noun, acceptable the adjective, accepted the seal of approval.
normal.cn: acceptance 是名词，acceptable 是形容词，accepted 是认可的印章。

abstract.en: Accepting is not wanting: the hand closes on what it did not choose.
abstract.cn: 接受不等于想要：手合拢在一个并非自己挑选的东西上。

abstract.en: A mind that accepts a fact is doing what the palm does with rain.
abstract.cn: 接受一个事实的心，做的是掌心承接雨水的事。

abstract.en: Every acceptance leaves a small mark of the one who did the taking.
abstract.cn: 每一次接受都留下做这件接取之事的人的一点痕迹。

examples.en: She accepted the invitation to dinner.
examples.cn: 她接受了晚餐的邀请。

examples.en: It took him years to accept his father's decision.
examples.cn: 他花了好几年才接受父亲的决定。

examples.en: Credit cards are accepted at most shops here.
examples.cn: 这里多数商店接受信用卡付款。

dict_mnemonic.text: ac-（向）+ cept（拿）= 朝自己这边拿过来 → 接受

root: 拉丁语 capere（拿取）加 ad-（朝向）→ accipere（取到自己这里）；同族词有 acceptance、acceptable、receive、capture、except。

sensesIntro.en: Accept begins with a hand taking a gift and ends with a person taking a hard fact without protest.
sensesIntro.cn: accept 从手接过礼物开始，到人无抗辩地接下一个艰难事实为止。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands closing on what arrives.
core.cn: 核心意象：双手合拢在到来的东西上。

branches.en: HAND LINE: the object is received.
branches.cn: 手线：物件被收下。

branches.en: WORD LINE: a proposal is answered yes.
branches.cn: 言语线：提议得到答应。

branches.en: MIND LINE: a statement is held as true.
branches.cn: 心智线：一句话被当作真。

branches.en: BURDEN LINE: hardship is taken without protest.
branches.cn: 重负线：困难被无抗辩地承受。

branches.en: CONTRAST: except leaves one out, accept takes one in.
branches.cn: 对照线：except 排除一个，accept 接进一个。

intro.en: A prefix of direction on a Latin root of taking.
intro.cn: 一个表方向的前缀加拉丁「拿取」词根。

latinIntro.en: Ad- plus capere gives accipere, to take to oneself, the ancestor of the verb.
latinIntro.cn: ad- 加 capere 得到 accipere「取到自己这里」，即动词的祖先。

items.exampleCN: 它也出现在 except 里。

definition_zh: 可以接受的；过得去的；合意的
definition_en: good enough to be agreed to, though not perfect
core_image: 一件衣服有线头，但穿上出门也没人挑剔
scene: 房东看了看墙上的小洞，说这点损伤还算过得去。A short delay is acceptable if you call ahead.
sceneCN: 这里 acceptable 是「可以接受的」（第 1 个义项：虽不完美但能被认可）；句意是提前打电话的话，短时延误是可以接受的。

pos.zh: 形容词：可以接受的；过得去的；合意的

derivatives.zh: 反义词，义为「不可接受的」

senses.title: Good enough to be agreed to
senses.titleCN: 可以接受：虽不完美但能认可
senses.definition: of a standard that others are willing to approve
senses.definitionCN: 达到别愿意认可的标准
senses.example: The offer was acceptable to both sides.
senses.exampleCN: 这个提议双方都能接受。
senses.why: The -able ending says a thing can be accepted, so the bar is agreement, not perfection.
senses.whyCN: -able 词尾表示「能被接受」，所以标准是获认可，而非完美。

senses.title: Allowed by custom
senses.titleCN: 合规矩：社会习俗所容许
senses.definition: fitting the rules or manners of a group
senses.definitionCN: 符合某个群体的规矩或礼节
senses.example: Loud music is not acceptable at a funeral.
senses.exampleCN: 葬礼上放吵闹的音乐是不合规矩的。
senses.why: Groups set the bar, and what passes it becomes acceptable in that place.
senses.whyCN: 标准由群体设定，过关的东西在那个场合就算合宜。

senses.title: Merely passable
senses.titleCN: 勉强过得去：只是不至于不行
senses.definition: not good but not bad enough to complain about
senses.definitionCN: 不算好，但也没差到该抱怨
senses.example: The meal was acceptable, nothing more.
senses.exampleCN: 这顿饭还过得去，仅此而已。
senses.why: Acceptable can be warm approval or faint praise, and tone decides which.
senses.whyCN: acceptable 可以是热情的认可，也可以是勉强的肯定，语气决定是哪一种。

intro.en: Acceptable joins accept, from Latin accipere, to receive, with the Latin ending -abilis, able to be.
intro.cn: acceptable 由 accept（来自拉丁语 accipere「接收」）加拉丁词尾 -abilis「能够被…的」构成。

items.en: Accipere meant to take something to oneself.
items.cn: accipere 意为「把东西取到自己这里」。

items.en: The ending -abilis turned verbs into words for what can be done.
items.cn: -abilis 把动词变成表示「可被…」的词。

items.en: Old French acceptable carried the sense of pleasing and worthy of approval.
items.cn: 古法语 acceptable 带有「合意、值得认可」之意。

items.en: English used acceptable for what could be received with approval.
items.cn: 英语早期用 acceptable 指能被认可接收的东西。

items.en: The word now also covers things that are only just good enough.
items.cn: 这个词如今也指仅仅刚够格的东西。

note.en: The look-alike group builds on accept and its -able family; the near-meaning group holds words of sufficiency.
note.cn: 形近组由 accept 与其 -able 家族构成；近义组收表示够格的词。

entries.definition: The verb of taking what is offered.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「接受」。

entries.definition: Not good enough to be agreed to.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不可接受的」。

entries.definition: A way in or a right to enter; the ending differs.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「进入、通道」，词尾不同。

entries.definition: Meeting the requirement, a slightly stronger word.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「令人满意的」，语气略强。

entries.definition: Barely endurable, closer to the third sense.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「尚可忍受的」，接近第三义项。

entries.definition: Allowed to be brought in, especially as evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可采纳的」，多用于证据。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the able ending, the approval bar and the faint-praise tone.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借 -able 词尾、认可的门槛与勉强的语气。

normal.en: Accept is the verb, and -able makes it a quality a thing can carry.
normal.cn: accept 是动词，-able 把接受变成一种可以被携带的性质。

normal.en: Acceptable means the bar of agreement is met, not that the thing is admired.
normal.cn: acceptable 指达到了认可的门槛，而不是被赞赏。

normal.en: Unacceptable is the same word with a lid on top, refusing entry.
normal.cn: unacceptable 是同一个词加了盖子，拒绝进入。

normal.en: Socially acceptable asks who set the rules of that place.
normal.cn: socially acceptable 问的是那个场合由谁定规矩。

normal.en: In job ads, acceptable often sits exactly where good enough sits.
normal.cn: 招聘广告里，acceptable 常常正坐在「够格」的位置上。

abstract.en: An acceptable thing lives between wanting and refusing.
abstract.cn: 可接受之物居于想要与拒绝之间。

abstract.en: The bar is set by others, which is why the word so often sounds like a verdict.
abstract.cn: 门槛由别人设定，所以这个词听起来常常像一份判决。

abstract.en: Tolerated is the quiet cousin, and acceptable still keeps a little more approval in it.
abstract.cn: tolerated 是它安静的近亲，而 acceptable 里还留着一点认可。

examples.en: The plan was acceptable to every member of the team.
examples.cn: 这个方案团队里每个人都能接受。

examples.en: Some noise is acceptable in a shared flat.
examples.cn: 合住的公寓里有点声音是能接受的。

examples.en: His work was acceptable but never outstanding.
examples.cn: 他的工作还算过关，却从不突出。

dict_mnemonic.text: accept（接受）+ -able（可…的）= 可被接受的

root: accept（拉丁语 accipere「接收」）+ -able（可…的）；同族词有 acceptance、acceptability、unacceptable。

sensesIntro.en: Acceptable names the line above refusal and below praise, and the three senses stand on that line.
sensesIntro.cn: acceptable 指的是「拒绝之上、赞赏之下」的那道线，三个义项都站在这条线上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a garment with a loose thread that still passes the door.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件带线头的衣服，仍能穿出门。

branches.en: AGREE LINE: the offer is approved.
branches.cn: 认可线：提议获通过。

branches.en: CUSTOM LINE: the group sets the bar.
branches.cn: 惯例线：群体设定门槛。

branches.en: PRAISE LINE: the praise is faint.
branches.cn: 褒贬线：称赞只有一点点。

branches.en: CONTRAST: acceptable passes, unacceptable is shut out.
branches.cn: 对照线：acceptable 过关，unacceptable 被关在门外。

branches.en: TONE LINE: the same word can approve warmly or barely.
branches.cn: 语气线：同一个词可以热情认可，也可以勉强点头。

intro.en: A Latin verb of receiving plus the ending that marks what can be done.
intro.cn: 一个拉丁「接收」动词，加上表示「可被…」的词尾。

latinIntro.en: The ending -abilis attached to accipere produced the ancestor of acceptable.
latinIntro.cn: -abilis 加在 accipere 上，产生了 acceptable 的祖先。

definition_en: the act of taking something offered, or the state of being admitted by others
core_image: 一张签发好的文件上盖了章，从此这件事正式算数
scene: 录取通知寄到那天，全家人围着那张纸看。Her acceptance into the group changed how she saw herself.
sceneCN: 这里 acceptance 是「接纳」（第 2 个义项：被某个群体承认并收进来）；句意是被这个群体接纳改变了她对自己的看法。

pos.zh: 名词：接受；接纳；赞同；承认

senses.title: Act of taking an offer
senses.titleCN: 接受：把提议或物品收下
senses.definition: the act of agreeing to receive what is offered
senses.definitionCN: 同意收下所提供之物的行为
senses.example: His acceptance of the cheque ended the dispute.
senses.exampleCN: 他收下了那张支票，纠纷就此结束。
senses.why: The noun names the closing of the hand on an offer.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词命名的是手在提议上合拢的那一动作。

senses.title: Being admitted by others
senses.titleCN: 接纳：被别人承认并收进来
senses.definition: the state of being welcomed into a group
senses.definitionCN: 被某个群体欢迎并接纳的状态
senses.example: Her acceptance into the club surprised no one.
senses.exampleCN: 她被俱乐部接纳，没人感到意外。
senses.why: Here the subject is passive: the group does the taking in.
senses.whyCN: 此处主语是被动的一方：做「收进来」动作的是群体。

senses.title: General approval
senses.titleCN: 认同：广泛的赞同
senses.definition: the fact of being approved by many people
senses.definitionCN: 被许多人赞同的事实
senses.example: The method found wide acceptance.
senses.exampleCN: 这个方法获得了广泛认同。
senses.why: When many hands close at once, the word means approval in public.
senses.whyCN: 当许多只手同时合上时，这个词就指公开的赞同。

senses.title: Quiet recognition of a fact
senses.titleCN: 默默承受：对事实的默认
senses.definition: the process of coming to terms with something hard
senses.definitionCN: 逐步与艰难事实达成和解的过程
senses.example: Her acceptance of the illness took months.
senses.exampleCN: 她接受这个病花了几个月。
senses.why: The word turns inward and slow when it names a private reckoning.
senses.whyCN: 当它命名一次内心的清算时，这个词转向内，而且变慢。

intro.en: Acceptance comes from Latin acceptantia, a taking, built on accipere, to receive.
intro.cn: acceptance 来自拉丁语 acceptantia「接受」，构于 accipere「接收」之上。

items.en: Accipere meant to take something to oneself.
items.cn: accipere 意为「把东西取到自己这里」。

items.en: Medieval Latin acceptantia named the act of receiving or approving.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 acceptantia 指接收或认可的行为。

items.en: Old French accepter carried the same sense into everyday use.
items.cn: 古法语 accepter 把同样的意思带进日常用法。

items.en: English acceptance first meant a favourable receiving of a thing.
items.cn: 英语 acceptance 起初指对事物的欣然接收。

items.en: The word grew to cover being admitted and coming to terms with facts.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到指被接纳以及与事实和解。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -ance family; the near-meaning group holds words of approval.
note.cn: 形近组共用 -ance 家族；近义组收表示认可的词。

entries.definition: The verb of taking what is offered.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「接受」，名词即由它而来。

entries.definition: The quality of passing the bar.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「可接受性」。

entries.definition: One who accepts, as in a bill of exchange.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「接受人」，多见于汇票。

entries.definition: A judgement that something is good.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「批准、赞同」。

entries.definition: Being allowed to enter a place or group.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「准入、进入」，接近第二义项。

entries.definition: Public notice that a thing counts.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「认可」，偏公开。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the -ance noun ending, the letter of offer and the quiet sense.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借 -ance 名词词尾、录取信与那层安静的义。

normal.en: Add -ance to accept and the act becomes a thing you can receive.
normal.cn: accept 后加 -ance，那个动作就变成可以收到的东西。

normal.en: Letter of acceptance is the envelope that says the door is open.
normal.cn: letter of acceptance 就是那封说门已打开的信。

normal.en: Acceptance cuts both ways: you take something, or a group takes you.
normal.cn: acceptance 是双向的：你收下东西，或者群体收下你。

normal.en: Wide acceptance is measured in hands that closed, not in one voice.
normal.cn: wide acceptance 以合拢的手来衡量，而非以一个人的声音。

normal.en: Acceptance of a hard fact is the slowest sense of the word.
normal.cn: acceptance of a hard fact 是这个词最慢的一层义。

abstract.en: A thing is accepted twice: once into a hand, once into a common mind.
abstract.cn: 一件事被接受两次：一次被收进手中，一次被收进共同的心思。

abstract.en: Admission asks who let you in; acceptance asks whether you belong.
abstract.cn: 准入问的是谁放你进来，接纳问的是你属不属于这里。

abstract.en: Accepting what cannot change is not surrender but a change of footing.
abstract.cn: 接受无法改变之事不是投降，而是换了一个立足点。

examples.en: She sent in her acceptance within a week.
examples.cn: 她在一周内寄去了接受函。

examples.en: The new method slowly gained acceptance among teachers.
examples.cn: 新方法渐渐得到了教师们的认同。

examples.en: His acceptance of the blame surprised his colleagues.
examples.cn: 他认下这份责任，让同事们很意外。

dict_mnemonic.text: accept（接受）+ -ance（名词）= 接受这件事本身

root: 拉丁语 accipere（接收）+ -antia（名词词尾）→ acceptantia；同族词有 accept、acceptable、accepted。

sensesIntro.en: Acceptance names both sides of a handshake, the taking and the being taken in.
sensesIntro.cn: acceptance 命名一次握手的双方：收下别人，和被别人收下。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stamped paper that makes a thing count from now on.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚盖章，让一件事从此刻起算数。

branches.en: OFFER LINE: the goods or the offer is taken.
branches.cn: 提议线：物品或提议被收下。

branches.en: DOOR LINE: the group lets a person in.
branches.cn: 门线：群体放一个人进来。

branches.en: PUBLIC LINE: many approve at once.
branches.cn: 公众线：许多人同时赞同。

branches.en: INNER LINE: a hard fact is slowly let in.
branches.cn: 内心线：艰难事实被慢慢让进来。

branches.en: CONTRAST: refusal looks the same from both sides of the door.
branches.cn: 对照线：拒绝在门的这两侧看出去长得一样。

intro.en: A Latin verb of receiving with the noun ending that names the act.
intro.cn: 一个拉丁「接收」动词加上命名这一行为的名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Accipere plus -antia gave acceptantia, the Medieval Latin source of the English noun.
latinIntro.cn: accipere 加 -antia 得到 acceptantia，是英语名词的中世纪拉丁语来源。

definition_zh: 通道；接近的机会；使用权；存取
definition_en: a way to reach or enter a place, or the right to use something
core_image: 一扇门开着一条缝，门后是本来进不去的地方
scene: 档案馆的门平时锁着，只有带着证件的人才被放进去。Students have free access to the library after six.
sceneCN: 这里 access 是「使用权、接近的机会」（第 2 个义项：可以使用某物的权利）；句意是六点以后学生可免费使用图书馆。

pos.zh: 名词：通道；接近的机会；使用权；存取
动词：进入；访问；存取

derivatives.zh: 义为「可接近的、可使用的」

senses.title: A way in
senses.titleCN: 通道：进入的路径
senses.definition: a route by which a place can be reached
senses.definitionCN: 可以抵达某处的路线
senses.example: The only access to the farm is a dirt track.
senses.exampleCN: 通往农场只有一条土路。
senses.why: Latin accessus was a coming near, and a path is what makes nearness possible.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 accessus 意为「靠近」，而路径正是让靠近成为可能的东西。

senses.title: The chance to use
senses.titleCN: 使用权：可以使用某物的机会
senses.definition: the opportunity or right to use something
senses.definitionCN: 使用某物的机会或权利
senses.example: Every student has access to the labs.
senses.exampleCN: 每个学生都能使用实验室。
senses.why: When the thing reached is not a place but a service, access becomes permission.
senses.whyCN: 当抵达的不是地点而是服务时，access 就变成许可。

senses.title: The act of reaching
senses.titleCN: 进入：实际接近的动作
senses.definition: the act of getting to a person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 抵达某人或某物的行为本身
senses.example: Access to the patient is limited to family.
senses.exampleCN: 探视这位病人只限家属。
senses.why: The noun can name the act rather than the right, and then it is a gate keeper's word.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词可以指行为而非权利，此时它是门卫的词。

senses.title: Finding stored data
senses.titleCN: 存取：从库中取出数据
senses.definition: the act of reaching and reading stored information
senses.definitionCN: 抵达并读取已存信息的行为
senses.example: Access to the files is logged by hour.
senses.exampleCN: 读取这些档案的时间会被记录。
senses.why: Computing borrowed the word for the reaching of stored data.
senses.whyCN: 计算领域借这个词表示对已存数据的抵达。

intro.en: Access comes from Latin accessus, a coming near, from accedere, to go toward.
intro.cn: access 来自拉丁语 accessus「走近」，源自动词 accedere「走向」。

items.en: Cedere meant to go or yield, and it underlies proceed and recession.
items.cn: cedere 意为「走、让步」，也是 proceed 与 recession 的底层词。

items.en: Accedere meant to go toward something, to come near.
items.cn: accedere 意为「向某处走」，即走近。

items.en: Accessus named the approach itself and the right to approach.
items.cn: accessus 指接近本身，也指接近的权利。

items.en: English access meant the act of drawing near a person or place.
items.cn: 英语 access 起初指靠某人或某地的行为。

items.en: Computing gave the word the sense of reaching stored data.
items.cn: 计算领域赋予这个词「读取已存数据」之义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the ac- prefix or the -cess root; the near-meaning group holds words of getting in.
note.cn: 形近组共用 ac- 前缀或 -cess 词根；近义组收表示进入的词。

entries.definition: Easy to approach or use.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可接近的」。

entries.definition: Too much of something; the prefix points outward.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「过量」，前缀方向相反。

entries.definition: To judge the value of something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「评估」，拼写相近而意义不同。

entries.definition: The act of going in through a door.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「进入、入口」，偏具体。

entries.definition: Permission to enter a building or an event.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「准入」，偏许可。

entries.definition: The act of moving nearer to something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「接近」，最贴近词源的一层。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the go-toward root, the key-card and the stored-data sense.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借「走向」词根、门禁卡与数据存取的那层义。

normal.en: Access and proceed share a root of going: access is going toward a door.
normal.cn: access 与 proceed 共用「走」的词根：access 就是朝一扇门走。

normal.en: Have access to is the phrase behind nearly every sentence with this noun.
normal.cn: have access to 几乎是这个名词所有句子背后的短语。

normal.en: A key card is access made of plastic.
normal.cn: 门禁卡是用塑料做成的 access。

normal.en: Excess has the same -cess but a prefix that pushes out.
normal.cn: excess 词尾相同，但前缀把东西往外推。

normal.en: In computing, access means reaching files without touching them.
normal.cn: 在计算领域，access 指不碰实物就能取到文件。

abstract.en: Access is not a place but the short distance between you and it.
abstract.cn: access 不是一个地方，而是你与它之间那一小段距离。

abstract.en: Every door has two sides, and the noun can name either the door or the right.
abstract.cn: 每扇门都有两侧，这个名词可以指门本身，也可指进门的权利。

abstract.en: What is accessible stops being precious, which is why the word so often means power.
abstract.cn: 可及之物便不再珍贵，所以这个词常常意味着权力。

examples.en: The hotel has direct access to the beach.
examples.cn: 这家酒店可以直接走到海滩。

examples.en: You need a password to access your account.
examples.cn: 访问账户需要密码。

examples.en: Only staff have access to these records.
examples.cn: 只有员工才能查阅这些记录。

dict_mnemonic.text: ac-（向）+ cess（走）= 朝那边走过去 → 接近、进入

root: 拉丁语 cedere（走）加 ad-（朝向）→ accedere（走近），名词 accessus；同族词有 accessible、accession、excess、proceed。

sensesIntro.en: Access starts as a path, then becomes a right, then an act, and finally a way of reaching data.
sensesIntro.cn: access 先是路径，再成为权利，再成为动作，最后成为抵达数据的方式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a door left ajar into a room you may not enter.
core.cn: 核心意象：门留了一条缝，门后本来进不去。

branches.en: PATH LINE: the physical way in.
branches.cn: 路径线：实际的通道。

branches.en: RIGHT LINE: permission to use.
branches.cn: 权利线：使用的许可。

branches.en: ACT LINE: the reaching itself.
branches.cn: 行为线：抵达的动作本身。

branches.en: DATA LINE: files reached in a system.
branches.cn: 数据线：系统里的档案被取到。

branches.en: CONTRAST: to deny access is to close the path and the right at once.
branches.cn: 对照线：deny access 同时关掉路径与权利。

intro.en: A prefix of direction with a Latin root of going, and a noun of approach.
intro.cn: 一个表方向的前缀加拉丁「走」词根，构成一个「接近」的名词。

latinIntro.en: Ad- plus cedere gave accedere, to go toward, and its noun accessus.
latinIntro.cn: ad- 加 cedere 得 accedere「走向」，其名词为 accessus。

items.example: It points the going at a door.

items.exampleCN: 它也出现在 proceed 里。

items.meaning: a formal coming into a post

definition_en: something bad that happens by chance, with no one planning it
core_image: 路口两辆车轻轻碰在一起，谁也没打算这么做
scene: 雨天路滑，一辆车撞上了护栏，救护车很快赶到。He lost a finger in a workshop accident.
sceneCN: 这里 accident 是「事故」（第 1 个义项：造成损伤的意外事件）；句意是他在车间事故中失去了一根手指。

pos.zh: 名词：事故；意外；偶发事件

senses.title: An incident that harms
senses.titleCN: 事故：造成损失的意外事件
senses.definition: an unlucky event that causes injury or damage
senses.definitionCN: 造成伤害或损失的不幸事件
senses.example: There was an accident on the motorway this morning.
senses.exampleCN: 今早高速公路上出了事故。
senses.why: The Latin word meant something that falls on you, and a crash is what falls hardest.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁词指「落在你身上的事」，撞车正是落得最重的那种。

senses.title: Chance without plan
senses.titleCN: 偶然：无人计划的发生
senses.definition: the working of chance, with no design behind it
senses.definitionCN: 无人设计、纯由巧合造成
senses.example: I found the letter by accident.
senses.exampleCN: 我偶然找到了那封信。
senses.why: Here the same noun drops the harm and keeps only the absence of plan.
senses.whyCN: 这里同一个名词丢掉了伤害，只剩下「没有计划」这一点。

senses.title: An unplanned event at all
senses.titleCN: 偶发事件：不论好坏的不确定事
senses.definition: any event not arranged in advance
senses.definitionCN: 任何未事先安排的事
senses.example: Meeting her was a happy accident.
senses.exampleCN: 遇见她是件令人高兴的偶发事件。
senses.why: If chance can hurt, it can also please, and the word widens to cover both.
senses.whyCN: 巧合能伤人，也能带来喜悦，于是这个词扩到两者都包括。

intro.en: Accident comes from Latin accidere, to fall upon, from ad- plus cadere, to fall.
intro.cn: accident 来自拉丁语 accidere「落到身上」，由 ad- 加 cadere「落下」构成。

items.en: Cadere meant to fall, and it underlies cadence and decay.
items.cn: cadere 意为「落下」，也是 cadence 与 decay 的底层词。

items.en: Accidere meant to happen, literally to fall upon a person.
items.cn: accidere 意为「发生」，字面即「落在一人身上」。

items.en: Accidens named a quality that comes and goes, not part of the essence.
items.cn: accidens 指来去不定、非本质的属性。

items.en: English accident meant any chance event before it meant a crash.
items.cn: 英语 accident 先指任何偶然事件，后指车祸之类的意外。

items.en: Modern usage concentrates on harmful events and on by accident.
items.cn: 现代用法集中于有害事件与 by accident 这一短语。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the cad- fall root; the near-meaning group holds words of mishaps.
note.cn: 形近组共用 cad-「落下」词根；近义组收表示意外事故的词。

entries.definition: Happening by chance, not planned.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「意外的」。

entries.definition: In a way that was not planned.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「意外地」。

entries.definition: An event, often an unpleasant one; the prefix differs.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「事件」，前缀不同。

entries.definition: A violent collision, narrower than accident.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「撞车」，比 accident 窄。

entries.definition: A small unlucky event, lighter than accident.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「小意外」，语气较轻。

entries.definition: Two things meeting by chance, with no harm implied.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「巧合」，不含伤害。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the fall root, the by accident phrase and the happy accident sense.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借「落下」词根、by accident 短语与 happy accident 的用法。

normal.en: Accident shares a falling root with decay: something falls on you.
normal.cn: accident 与 decay 共用「落下」词根：有东西落到了你身上。

normal.en: By accident is the phrase that removes the blame and keeps only chance.
normal.cn: by accident 这个短语把责任拿掉，只留下巧合。

normal.en: Incident and accident differ by a prefix and by a hint of harm.
normal.cn: incident 与 accident 差着一个前缀，也差着一点伤害的暗示。

normal.en: Accident insurance covers the falling, not the planning.
normal.cn: 意外保险保的是那一下落下，不是计划。

normal.en: A happy accident is the word smiling for once.
normal.cn: a happy accident 是这个词难得地笑了一回。

abstract.en: An accident is what happens when a plan meets something it never saw.
abstract.cn: 事故是计划遇上一个它从未看见的东西时发生的事。

abstract.en: The word carries no agent: nobody chose it, and that absence is the meaning.
abstract.cn: 这个词不带施动者：没人选择它，这份空缺就是它的意义。

abstract.en: Chance can fall as harm or as gift, and the same noun holds both.
abstract.cn: 巧合可以落成伤害，也可以落成礼物，同一个名词装得下两者。

examples.en: The accident happened at the corner of the street.
examples.cn: 事故发生在街角。

examples.en: I deleted the file by accident.
examples.cn: 我不小心把文件删掉了。

examples.en: Their meeting was a pure accident of timing.
examples.cn: 他们的相遇纯粹是时间的巧合。

dict_mnemonic.text: ac-（向）+ cid（落）+ -ent（名词）= 落到身上的事 → 意外

root: 拉丁语 cadere（落下）加 ad-（朝向）→ accidere（落到身上、发生）；同族词有 accidental、accidentally、incident、cadence、decay。

sensesIntro.en: Accident first means whatever falls on a person, then the falling that hurts, then chance itself.
sensesIntro.cn: accident 先指落到人身上的任何事，再指伤人的那一下落下，再指巧合本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two cars touching at a corner nobody planned to meet at.
core.cn: 核心意象：两辆车在没人约好的路口碰上。

branches.en: HARM LINE: the falling hurts people or things.
branches.cn: 伤害线：这一下落伤了人或物。

branches.en: CHANCE LINE: no plan stands behind it.
branches.cn: 巧合线：背后没有计划。

branches.en: EVENT LINE: chance may also bring good.
branches.cn: 事件线：巧合也可能带来好事。

branches.en: REPORT LINE: police record the fall and ask who drove.
branches.cn: 记录线：警方记下这一下落并问谁在开车。

branches.en: CONTRAST: a coincidence is accident without the harm.
branches.cn: 对照线：coincidence 是没有伤害的 accident。

intro.en: A prefix of direction on a Latin root of falling.
intro.cn: 一个表方向的前缀加拉丁「落下」词根。

latinIntro.en: Ad- plus cadere produced accidere, to fall upon, the source of the noun.
latinIntro.cn: ad- 加 cadere 得 accidere「落到身上」，即名词的来源。

items.example: It aims the falling at a person.

items.exampleCN: 它也出现在 incident 里。

items.meaning: an event falling on a place

definition_zh: 意外的；偶然的；非本意的
definition_en: happening by chance and not planned or intended
core_image: 手肘一碰，桌上的杯子歪倒，谁都不是故意的
scene: 他本想按保存，手指却按到了旁边那个键。The fire was accidental, and no one was blamed.
sceneCN: 这里 accidental 是「意外的」（第 1 个义项：不是计划内的）；句意是这场火是意外造成的，没有人被责怪。

pos.zh: 形容词：意外的；偶然的；非本意的

senses.title: Not planned
senses.titleCN: 意外的：不在计划之内
senses.definition: happening without any plan behind it
senses.definitionCN: 背后没有任何计划而发生
senses.example: The damage was accidental, not deliberate.
senses.exampleCN: 这处损坏是意外造成的，并非故意。
senses.why: The adjective marks the absence of design; nothing arranged this.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词标记的是设计的缺席：没有任何东西安排它。

senses.title: Not intended by the doer
senses.titleCN: 非本意的：行动者并不想如此
senses.definition: done without the wish to do it
senses.definitionCN: 做事的人并不希望这样发生
senses.example: An accidental touch sent the vase to the floor.
senses.exampleCN: 无意中一碰，花瓶落到了地上。
senses.why: Chance can enter through a person's own hand, and then the word defends them.
senses.whyCN: 巧合也可能从当事人自己的手中进来，此时这个词为他辩护。

senses.title: Happening to be so
senses.titleCN: 偶合的：碰巧如此的属性
senses.definition: existing as a chance feature rather than an essence
senses.definitionCN: 作为偶然而非本质的特征存在
senses.example: The similarity between the names is accidental.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个名字相似是偶然的。
senses.why: Things can be alike without any reason, and the adjective says exactly that.
senses.whyCN: 事物可以无缘无故地相似，这个形容词说的正是这一点。

intro.en: Accidental is the adjective of accident, from Latin accidere, to fall upon.
intro.cn: accidental 是 accident 的形容词，源自拉丁语 accidere「落到身上」。

items.en: Accidens named a property that comes and goes without belonging to the essence.
items.cn: accidens 指来去不定、不属于本质的属性。

items.en: Medieval writers used accidental for what was not essential to a thing.
items.cn: 中世纪作者用 accidental 指对事物并非本质的部分。

items.en: Old French accidentel carried the sense of chance and mishap.
items.cn: 古法语 accidentel 带有偶然与不幸之意。

items.en: English accidental first meant not essential, then not intended.
items.cn: 英语 accidental 先指非本质，后指非本意。

items.en: Modern usage keeps the plain sense of happening by chance.
items.cn: 现代用法保留「偶然发生」这一朴素义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the accident family or the -al ending; the near-meaning group holds words of chance.
note.cn: 形近组共用 accident 家族或 -al 词尾；近义组收表示偶然的词。

entries.definition: The adverb, in a way not planned.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「意外地」。

entries.definition: The noun of a chance event.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「事故、意外」。

entries.definition: Happening as a minor side effect.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「附带的」，前缀不同。

entries.definition: Not meant by the person acting.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「非故意的」，接近第二义项。

entries.definition: Without pattern or choice at all.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「随机的」，比偶然更无规律。

entries.definition: The plain word for what happens without design.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「机会、偶然」，最朴素。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the -al ending, the not-intended sense and the strange-hobby sense.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借 -al 词尾、非本意的义项与「奇怪嗜好」的那层用法。

normal.en: Accident is the noun, and -al turns it into the quality of a happening.
normal.cn: accident 是名词，-al 把一次发生变成一种性质。

normal.en: Accidental damage is what insurance pays for because no one chose it.
normal.cn: accidental damage 是保险肯赔的，因为没人选择它。

normal.en: An accidental discovery is how penicillin arrived.
normal.cn: accidental discovery 正是青霉素被发现的方式。

normal.en: The adverb accidentally carries the same defence, one step away.
normal.cn: 副词 accidentally 带着同样的辩护，只差一步。

normal.en: Incidental looks close but means a side effect, not a surprise.
normal.cn: incidental 长得很近，但指副作用，而非意外。

abstract.en: What is accidental has no author, and the word quietly removes blame.
abstract.cn: 偶然之事没有作者，这个词悄悄取走了责备。

abstract.en: Chance features can look like essence until you ask why they are there.
abstract.cn: 偶然的特征看起来像本质，直到你问它为何在那里。

abstract.en: The accidental is what the plan did not reserve space for.
abstract.cn: 偶然之物就是计划没有为它留出空间的东西。

examples.en: The breakage was accidental and the shop replaced it.
examples.cn: 这次破损是意外造成的，店里给换了新的。

examples.en: Their resemblance is entirely accidental.
examples.cn: 他们的相像是完全偶然的。

examples.en: An accidental remark started the whole argument.
examples.cn: 一句无意中的话引发了整场争论。

dict_mnemonic.text: accident（意外）+ -al（…的）= 意外造成的

root: accident（拉丁语 accidere「落到身上」）+ -al（形容词词尾）；同族词有 accidentally、incidental、incident。

sensesIntro.en: Accidental names what no plan and no wish put there, whether in an event or in a likeness.
sensesIntro.cn: accidental 命名的是既无计划也无意愿放置的东西，无论出现在事件里还是相似里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an elbow nudges a cup and nobody meant it.
core.cn: 核心意象：手肘碰倒杯子，没人是故意的。

branches.en: PLAN LINE: nothing arranged it.
branches.cn: 计划线：没有任何安排。

branches.en: WISH LINE: the doer did not want it.
branches.cn: 意愿线：行动者并不想要。

branches.en: LIKENESS LINE: the resemblance has no cause.
branches.cn: 相似线：相像没有原因。

branches.en: INSURANCE LINE: the policy pays for the damage.
branches.cn: 保险线：保单赔付这类损坏。

branches.en: CONTRAST: incidental is a side effect, accidental is a surprise.
branches.cn: 对照线：incidental 是附带效果，accidental 是意外。

intro.en: The noun of a chance event with the adjective ending.
intro.cn: 一个偶然事件的名词加上形容词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Accidere, to fall upon, gave the noun accident and from it the adjective.
latinIntro.cn: accidere「落到身上」先得名词 accident，再由它得形容词。

items.example: It makes the noun an adjective.

definition_en: in a way that was not planned or not intended
core_image: 伸手去拿盐，手却把杯子推到了桌边
scene: 她转身时手肘碰到了托盘，杯子摔在地上。I accidentally sent the message to the wrong group.
sceneCN: 这里 accidentally 是「无意中」（第 1 个义项：不是有意的动作方式）；句意是我无意中把消息发错了群。

pos.zh: 副词：意外地；偶然地；无意中

forms.label: 无比较级变化（可用 more accidentally）

senses.title: Without meaning to
senses.titleCN: 无意中：动作不是有意的
senses.definition: doing something without the wish to do it
senses.definitionCN: 做了某事却没有那样的意愿
senses.example: I accidentally deleted the folder.
senses.exampleCN: 我误删了那个文件夹。
senses.why: The adverb answers how the deed was done, and the answer is: not on purpose.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词回答「这事怎么做成的」，答案是：并非故意。

senses.title: By pure chance
senses.titleCN: 偶然地：纯由巧合
senses.definition: through chance alone, with no hand involved
senses.definitionCN: 完全凭巧合，不涉及任何人的动作
senses.example: The two names were accidentally alike.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个名字偶然地相似。
senses.why: Here no one acts at all, and the adverb marks coincidence instead of mistake.
senses.whyCN: 此处根本没人在动作，副词标记的是巧合而非失误。

senses.title: Almost by design
senses.titleCN: 似无意实有意：装作不小心
senses.definition: done in a way that pretends to be a mistake
senses.definitionCN: 以一种假装失误的方式做出
senses.example: He accidentally left the file on her desk.
senses.exampleCN: 他「不经意地」把文件留在她桌上。
senses.why: The word can be borrowed as a cover, and then it carries irony.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以被借作掩护，此时便带上反讽。

intro.en: Accidentally is accident plus -al and -ly, from Latin accidere, to fall upon.
intro.cn: accidentally 由 accident 加 -al 与 -ly 构成，源自拉丁语 accidere「落到身上」。

items.en: Accidere meant to fall upon a person, and so to happen.
items.cn: accidere 意为「落到一人身上」，因此也指发生。

items.en: Accidentalis named what belongs to chance rather than essence.
items.cn: accidentalis 指属于偶然而非本质的东西。

items.en: Old French formed an adverb from accidentel in the same way.
items.cn: 古法语以同样方式从 accidentel 构成副词。

items.en: English built accidentally once the adjective was in place.
items.cn: 英语在形容词确立之后构成 accidentally。

items.en: The adverb settled into the apology of everyday speech.
items.cn: 这个副词定居在日常口语的道歉之中。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the accidental family; the near-meaning group holds words of unintended action.
note.cn: 形近组共用 accidental 家族；近义组收表示非故意动作的词。

entries.definition: Happening by chance, not planned.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「意外的」。

entries.definition: An event that happens without plan.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「事故」。

entries.definition: By the way, as a side remark.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「顺便一提」，前缀不同。

entries.definition: The everyday phrase for an unintended act.
entries.definitionCN: 短语，义为「错误地」，最日常。

entries.definition: Without any intention, a formal choice.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「非故意地」，较正式。

entries.definition: Without knowing what one was doing.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「不知不觉地」，多指不知情。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the -ly adverb ending, the wrong-group message and the ironic use.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借 -ly 副词词尾、发错群的消息与反讽用法。

normal.en: Accidental plus -ly makes the mistake an adverb, part of the doing.
normal.cn: accidental 加 -ly，让失误成为副词，进入动作的方式里。

normal.en: Accidentally sent it to the wrong group is the modern apology sentence.
normal.cn: 「accidentally sent it to the wrong group」是现代人的道歉句。

normal.en: By mistake is the plain phrase; accidentally is the more formal one.
normal.cn: by mistake 是日常短语，accidentally 更正式。

normal.en: Accidentally on purpose is the joke phrase that admits the design.
normal.cn: accidentally on purpose 是承认了故意的那句玩笑话。

normal.en: Incidentally looks close but means by the way.
normal.cn: incidentally 长得很近，但意思是「顺便一提」。

abstract.en: The adverb guards the doer: what happened did not come from the will.
abstract.cn: 这个副词守护着行动者：发生之事并非出自意愿。

abstract.en: Chance and mistake share this word, which is why it leaves room for excuses.
abstract.cn: 巧合与失误共用这个词，因此它给借口留了余地。

abstract.en: Saying accidentally is already asking to be read in a certain light.
abstract.cn: 说出 accidentally 本身就已经在请求别人用某种眼光读它。

examples.en: She accidentally knocked the phone off the table.
examples.cn: 她不小心把手机碰下了桌子。

examples.en: I accidentally took your umbrella this morning.
examples.cn: 我今天早上误拿了你的伞。

examples.en: The two designs were accidentally almost identical.
examples.cn: 这两个设计偶然地几乎一模一样。

dict_mnemonic.text: accidental（意外的）+ -ly（副词）= 意外地

root: accident（拉丁语 accidere「落到身上」）+ -al + -ly；同族词有 accidental、incidentally。

sensesIntro.en: Accidentally tells how an act went wrong, or that no one acted at all, and sometimes lets a person hide.
sensesIntro.cn: accidentally 说明一个动作如何出错，或根本没人在动作，有时还让人躲一躲。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand reaching for salt and knocking the cup.
core.cn: 核心意象：伸手拿盐，却把杯子碰倒。

branches.en: MISTAKE LINE: the act was not meant.
branches.cn: 失误线：动作并非有意。

branches.en: CHANCE LINE: no act at all, only coincidence.
branches.cn: 巧合线：根本没有动作，只有巧合。

branches.en: IRONY LINE: the mistake was arranged.
branches.cn: 反讽线：这个失误是被安排好的。

branches.en: CONTRAST: by mistake blames the act, accidentally softens it.
branches.cn: 对照线：by mistake 归责于动作，accidentally 把它软化。

branches.en: TONE LINE: the same adverb can defend or mock.
branches.cn: 语气线：同一个副词可以辩护，也可以嘲讽。

intro.en: Two suffixes turn a chance event into the manner of an action.
intro.cn: 两个词尾把一个偶然事件变成动作的方式。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root accidere reached English through accident, then accidental, then the adverb.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 accidere 经 accident、accidental 一路到副词。

definition_en: a place to stay or sleep, or the act of adjusting to fit a need
core_image: 旅馆前台的钥匙牌排成一列，每一块都等着有人来住
scene: 临时被派到外地三个月，公司先帮忙找了住处。Hotel accommodation is included in the price.
sceneCN: 这里 accommodation 是「住处」（第 1 个义项：可供住宿的地方）；句意是住宿已含在价格里。

pos.zh: 名词：住处；膳宿；住宿；调节

derivatives.zh: 义为「容纳、提供住宿、适应」
义为「住宿设施」，多用复数

senses.title: A place to stay
senses.titleCN: 住处：可供住宿的地方
senses.definition: a room or building where someone may stay
senses.definitionCN: 可供人停留居住的房间或建筑
senses.example: The price includes meals and accommodation.
senses.exampleCN: 价格含餐费与住宿。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to fit one thing to another, and a bed is fitted to a guest.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为「使一物适合另一物」，一张床就是配给房客的。

senses.title: Rooms and food together
senses.titleCN: 膳宿：住宿与餐饮的合称
senses.definition: lodging supplied along with meals
senses.definitionCN: 住宿连同餐食一并供给
senses.example: Full accommodation is offered on the farm.
senses.exampleCN: 农场提供全膳宿。
senses.why: Travellers needed both, so the noun came to bundle bed and board.
senses.whyCN: 旅人两样都需要，于是这个名词把床与饭捆在一起。

senses.title: Adjustment to a need
senses.titleCN: 调节：为适应而作的调整
senses.definition: the act of changing to suit a condition
senses.definitionCN: 为适合某种情况而作的改变
senses.example: The plan needed some accommodation to local rules.
senses.exampleCN: 方案需要对当地规定作些调整。
senses.why: Fitting returns as the abstract sense: people and rules adjust to each other.
senses.whyCN: 「配合」以抽象义回归：人与规则互相调整。

senses.title: A working agreement
senses.titleCN: 和解：双方勉强达成的共识
senses.definition: an arrangement reached between differing sides
senses.definitionCN: 意见不同各方勉强达成的安排
senses.example: The two parties reached an accommodation.
senses.exampleCN: 双方达成了和解。
senses.why: When two sides fit around each other, the noun names the fit itself.
senses.whyCN: 当两边互相让出形状时，这个名词命名的是这个形状。

intro.en: Accommodation comes from Latin accommodare, to fit to, from ad- plus commodus, suitable.
intro.cn: accommodation 来自拉丁语 accommodare「使适合」，由 ad- 加 commodus「合适的」构成。

items.en: Modus meant measure, and it underlies mode and modest.
items.cn: modus 意为「尺度」，也是 mode 与 modest 的底层词。

items.en: Commodus meant suitable or convenient, with com- adding fullness.
items.cn: commodus 意为「合适的、方便的」，com- 补充了「完全」之意。

items.en: Accommodare meant to fit one thing to another.
items.cn: accommodare 意为「把一物配到另一物上」。

items.en: French accommoder kept the sense of adjusting and of lodging.
items.cn: 法语 accommoder 保留了调整与留宿两义。

items.en: English accommodation grew into the everyday word for lodgings.
items.cn: 英语 accommodation 逐渐成为「住处」的日常说法。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the accommodate family; the near-meaning group holds words of lodging.
note.cn: 形近组共用 accommodate 家族；近义组收表示住宿的词。

entries.definition: To hold or to fit in with.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「容纳、适应」。

entries.definition: Willing to help others fit in.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「乐于助人的」。

entries.definition: Something that goes along with another.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「伴随物」，词形相近。

entries.definition: A place to sleep, often rented briefly.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「寄宿处」，多指短期。

entries.definition: Buildings for people to live in, a wider word.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「住房」，范围更广。

entries.definition: An agreement ending a dispute.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「和解」，接近第四义项。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the double m and c spelling, the fitting root and the hotel desk.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借双 m 双 c 的拼写、「配合」词根与酒店前台。

normal.en: Accommodation has two m and two c, and both doubles are easy to drop.
normal.cn: accommodation 有两个 m 和两个 c，这两处双写都容易漏。

normal.en: The root commodus means suitable, so the word is about fitting.
normal.cn: 词根 commodus 意为合适，所以这个词讲的是「配得上」。

normal.en: A bed fits the guest, and the noun names the bed that fits.
normal.cn: 床配上房客，这个名词命名的是那张配好的床。

normal.en: Student accommodation is the sign on the building near every campus.
normal.cn: student accommodation 是每所校园旁边楼上的那块牌子。

normal.en: Reach an accommodation means two sides each moved a little.
normal.cn: reach an accommodation 意思是两边各让了一点。

abstract.en: Lodging is adjustment made of walls: a room reshaped for someone else.
abstract.cn: 住宿是用墙壁做的调整：一间为别人重新塑形的房间。

abstract.en: A culture that accommodates makes space before anyone asks.
abstract.cn: 懂得配合的文化会在别人开口之前就留出空间。

abstract.en: Agreement is the same word in its abstract dress, two people fitting around each other.
abstract.cn: 和解是同一个词换上抽象的外衣：两个人绕出彼此的形状。

examples.en: The conference fee covers accommodation and two meals.
examples.cn: 会务费包含住宿和两餐。

examples.en: Many students struggle to find affordable accommodation.
examples.cn: 许多学生难以找到负担得起的住处。

examples.en: Both sides made an accommodation to end the strike.
examples.cn: 双方作出让步以结束罢工。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额靠门呆神」——来到门口靠一下，找个地方住下

root: 拉丁语 commodus（合适的）加 ad-（向）→ accommodare（使适合、安置）；同族词有 accommodate、accommodating、commodity、mode。

sensesIntro.en: Accommodation is always a fitting, whether of a bed to a guest or of two positions to each other.
sensesIntro.cn: accommodation 始终是一种「配适」，无论配的是床与客人，还是两个立场与彼此。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of key tags waiting for strangers.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排钥匙牌等着陌生人来住。

branches.en: ROOM LINE: a bed is fitted to a guest.
branches.cn: 房间线：床配给住客。

branches.en: BOARD LINE: bed and meals come together.
branches.cn: 餐宿线：床与饭一并供给。

branches.en: ADJUST LINE: people fit to rules.
branches.cn: 调整线：人配合规则。

branches.en: AGREEMENT LINE: two sides fit around each other.
branches.cn: 和解线：两边互相让出形状。

branches.en: CONTRAST: accommodation fits; confrontation does not.
branches.cn: 对照线：accommodation 相合，confrontation 相对。

intro.en: A prefix meaning toward on a Latin root of measure and suitability, with a noun ending.
intro.cn: 一个表「朝向」的前缀加拉丁「尺度、合适」词根，再接名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Ad- plus commodus, from modus, measure, gave accommodare, to fit to.
latinIntro.cn: ad- 加 commodus（源自 modus「尺度」）得到 accommodare「使适合」。

items.example: It points the fitting at a need.
items.exampleCN: 它把「配合」指向某个需要。
它也出现在 commodity 里。

definition_en: to go somewhere with someone, or to happen at the same time as something
core_image: 两个人并肩走，中间隔着半步，却始终没有分开
scene: 她去医院那天，弟弟一路跟着她，什么话也没多说。Thunder usually accompanies a heavy storm.
sceneCN: 这里 accompany 是「伴随」（第 3 个义项：与某事同时发生）；句意是雷声通常伴随强烈风暴而来。

pos.zh: 动词：陪伴；陪同；伴随；为…伴奏

derivatives.zh: 同根名词，义为「陪伴、公司」

senses.title: To go along with a person
senses.titleCN: 陪伴：与人同行
senses.definition: to travel or go somewhere together with someone
senses.definitionCN: 与某人一同前往某处
senses.example: Her brother accompanied her to the hospital.
senses.exampleCN: 她弟弟陪她去了医院。
senses.why: Latin com- means with, and panis means bread: the first companion shared bread.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 com- 意为「一起」，panis 意为「面包」：最初的同伴共享面包。

senses.title: To escort as a duty
senses.titleCN: 陪同：出于礼节或职责相陪
senses.definition: to go with someone in an official or polite role
senses.definitionCN: 以正式或礼貌的身份相随
senses.example: A guide accompanied the visitors through the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 一位向导陪参观者穿过大厅。
senses.why: The same going along can become a role, and then the verb is about position.
senses.whyCN: 同样的同行可以成为一种角色，此时这个动词讲的是位次。

senses.title: To happen at the same time
senses.titleCN: 伴随：与某事同时发生
senses.definition: to occur together with something else
senses.definitionCN: 与另一事物同时出现
senses.example: Fever often accompanies the infection.
senses.exampleCN: 发热常常伴随这种感染。
senses.why: The pair can be events rather than people, and the verb then means co-occurrence.
senses.whyCN: 同行的双方可以是事件而非人，动词于是指「同时出现」。

senses.title: To play music for
senses.titleCN: 伴奏：为演唱者或独奏者配乐
senses.definition: to play music that supports another performer
senses.definitionCN: 为另一位表演者演奏支撑性的音乐
senses.example: A pianist accompanied the young violinist.
senses.exampleCN: 一位钢琴家为这位年轻小提琴手伴奏。
senses.why: Music walks alongside a voice, which is the same picture with sound.
senses.whyCN: 音乐与一条人声并行，这是同一幅画面加上了声音。

intro.en: Accompany comes from Old French acompaignier, to be a companion, from com- plus panis, bread.
intro.cn: accompany 来自古法语 acompaignier「作同伴」，源自 com-（一起）加 panis（面包）。

items.en: Panis meant bread, and it survives in pantry and pannier.
items.cn: panis 意为「面包」，也留在 pantry 与 pannier 里。

items.en: Companio named one who shares bread with another.
items.cn: companio 指与别人共享面包的人。

items.en: Acompaignier meant to join someone as a companion.
items.cn: acompaignier 意为「作为同伴与人同行」。

items.en: English accompany kept both going along and, later, playing music for.
items.cn: 英语 accompany 既保留同行之义，后又增添伴奏之义。

items.en: The verb now also covers things that happen together.
items.cn: 这个动词如今也覆盖同时发生的事物。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the companion family; the near-meaning group holds words of going along.
note.cn: 形近组共用 companion 家族；近义组收表示同行的词。

entries.definition: Something that goes with another thing.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「伴随物、伴奏」。

entries.definition: A person who goes along with you.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「同伴」，同根。

entries.definition: Being with others, and later a firm.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「陪伴、公司」，同根。

entries.definition: To go with someone as a guard or guide.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「护送」，接近第二义项。

entries.definition: To be present with someone in a serving role.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「随侍、出席」，较正式。

entries.definition: The plain phrase for going along.
entries.definitionCN: 短语，义为「一起去」，最日常。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the shared-bread root, the hospital walk and the pianist.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借「共享面包」词根、去医院的那段路与钢琴伴奏。

normal.en: Accompany and companion share the bread root: those who eat together walk together.
normal.cn: accompany 与 companion 共用面包词根：一起吃饭的人一起走路。

normal.en: Be accompanied by is the passive phrase used in forms and police reports.
normal.cn: be accompanied by 是表格与警方记录里的被动短语。

normal.en: A pianist accompanies a singer the way a brother accompanies a sister.
normal.cn: 钢琴家陪伴歌手，就像弟弟陪伴姐姐。

normal.en: Double the c, keep the single n in the middle: a ccompany has two c.
normal.cn: 开头双 c，中间单 n：accompany 首部有两个 c。

normal.en: Fever accompanies infection, and now the word is about events.
normal.cn: fever accompanies infection，此时这个词说的是事件。

abstract.en: To accompany is to lend your presence without taking the lead.
abstract.cn: 陪伴是借出你的在场，而不去占据主导。

abstract.en: Bread shared became steps shared, and then notes played under a voice.
abstract.cn: 共享的面包变成共享的脚步，而后又变成在人声之下弹奏的音符。

abstract.en: Some things accompany others simply by happening in the same weather.
abstract.cn: 有些事只是因为在同一片天气里发生，便算作伴随。

examples.en: Children must be accompanied by an adult.
examples.cn: 儿童须由成人陪同。

examples.en: A nurse accompanied him to the operating room.
examples.cn: 一名护士陪他去了手术室。

examples.en: Dry weather accompanied the harvest that year.
examples.cn: 那年收割时一直伴着干燥的天气。

dict_mnemonic.text: ac-（向）+ company（同伴）= 跟着同伴走 → 陪伴

root: 拉丁语 panis（面包）加 com-（一起）→ companio（同吃面包的人）；经古法语 acompaignier 进入英语。同族词有 companion、company、accompaniment。

sensesIntro.en: Accompany moves from people sharing a road to events sharing a time to a piano sharing a melody.
sensesIntro.cn: accompany 从共走一路的人，走到共处一时的事件，再走到共奏一调的钢琴。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two people half a step apart, never separating.
core.cn: 核心意象：两人半步之隔，始终没有分开。

branches.en: WALK LINE: a friend goes along.
branches.cn: 同行线：朋友一起走。

branches.en: ROLE LINE: a guide goes along by duty.
branches.cn: 角色线：向导按职责同行。

branches.en: WEATHER LINE: two events arrive together.
branches.cn: 天气线：两件事一同到来。

branches.en: MUSIC LINE: notes walk beside a voice.
branches.cn: 音乐线：音符在歌声旁边走。

branches.en: CONTRAST: accompany means beside, not ahead.
branches.cn: 对照线：accompany 是在身旁，不在前面。

intro.en: A prefix meaning together with a Latin word for bread, through a French verb.
intro.cn: 一个表「一同」的前缀加拉丁「面包」一词，经法语动词进入英语。

latinIntro.en: Com- plus panis gave companio, one who shares bread, and the French verb followed.
latinIntro.cn: com- 加 panis 得 companio「共食面包者」，法语动词随之而来。

items.example: It links the going to a person.
items.exampleCN: 它把「走」连到一个人身上。
它也出现在 companion 里。

definition_en: to finish something successfully after effort
core_image: 清单上最后一项被划掉，笔尖在纸上停了一下
scene: 他们熬了三个通宵，终于在期限前把整份报告交了上去。She accomplished more in one year than others do in three.
sceneCN: 这里 accomplish 是「完成」（第 1 个义项：把一件事做成）；句意是她一年里做成的事比别人三年还多。

pos.zh: 动词：完成；实现；达到

senses.title: To complete a task
senses.titleCN: 完成：把一件事做完
senses.definition: to bring a piece of work to its end
senses.definitionCN: 把一项工作做到终点
senses.example: They accomplished the repairs before dark.
senses.exampleCN: 他们天黑前完成了修理。
senses.why: Latin complere means to fill up; the work is filled to the brim and stops.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 complere 意为「填满」，工作被填到满，然后停下。

senses.title: To reach a goal
senses.titleCN: 实现：达到预定目标
senses.definition: to achieve something aimed at
senses.definitionCN: 达到原先设定的目标
senses.example: The team accomplished what it set out to do.
senses.exampleCN: 团队实现了当初定下的目标。
senses.why: A goal is an end held in advance, and to accomplish it is to arrive there.
senses.whyCN: 目标是事先握住的终点，accomplish 就是抵达那里。

senses.title: To do something worth noting
senses.titleCN: 做成：做出值得称道的事
senses.definition: to perform something of value or scale
senses.definitionCN: 做出有价值或有规模的事情
senses.example: He accomplished a great deal in his short life.
senses.exampleCN: 他短暂一生中做成的事很多。
senses.why: The object here is not a task but a record, and the verb measures worth.
senses.whyCN: 此处对象不是任务而是成绩，动词衡量的是价值。

intro.en: Accomplish comes from Old French acomplir, from Latin complere, to fill up completely.
intro.cn: accomplish 来自古法语 acomplir，上溯拉丁语 complere「填满」。

items.en: Plere meant to fill, and it also underlies complete and supply.
items.cn: plere 意为「填满」，也是 complete 与 supply 的底层词。

items.en: Complere meant to fill something completely, to finish it.
items.cn: complere 意为「把某物完全填满」，即完成。

items.en: Acomplir meant to fulfil or to carry through.
items.cn: acomplir 意为「履行、贯彻到底」。

items.en: English accomplish meant to fulfil a duty or a promise.
items.cn: 英语 accomplish 起初指履行义务或承诺。

items.en: The verb widened to any task brought to success.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到任何被做成的事。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -plish or -plish sounding root; the near-meaning group holds words of finishing.
note.cn: 形近组共用 -plish 音形；近义组收表示完成的词。

entries.definition: An achievement or the act of finishing.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「成就、完成」。

entries.definition: Skilled, or fully done.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「精通的、已完成的」。

entries.definition: To finish or to make whole.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「完成」，同根。

entries.definition: To reach a goal by effort, close to the second sense.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「实现」，接近第二义项。

entries.definition: To carry out a promise or a duty fully.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「履行」，偏义务。

entries.definition: The plain phrase for doing a plan.
entries.definitionCN: 短语，义为「执行」，最日常。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the fill-up root, the crossed-out list and the accomplished adjective.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借「填满」词根、划掉的清单与 accomplished 这一形容词。

normal.en: Accomplish shares a filling root with complete: the work is filled to the brim.
normal.cn: accomplish 与 complete 共用「填满」词根：工作被填到沿口。

normal.en: Double c, one m, then -plish: a common spelling trap.
normal.cn: 首部双 c、单 m，再接 -plish：常见拼写陷阱。

normal.en: An accomplished pianist is one whose practice is already complete.
normal.cn: an accomplished pianist 指练琴已经到家的人。

normal.en: Accomplish a task is the office phrase; accomplish a goal is the school one.
normal.cn: accomplish a task 是办公室说法，accomplish a goal 是学校里说法。

normal.en: Accomplishment is the noun you put on a form that asks what you did.
normal.cn: accomplishment 是表上「你做过什么」那一栏要填的名词。

abstract.en: What is accomplished is not merely done but done to the end.
abstract.cn: 被 accomplish 的事不只是做了，而是做到了尽头。

abstract.en: A list is a row of empty vessels, and the verb fills them one by one.
abstract.cn: 清单是一排空容器，这个动词一只一只地填满。

abstract.en: The word asks for effort, which is why it rarely describes anything easy.
abstract.cn: 这个词要求付出，因此很少用来描述轻松的事。

examples.en: We accomplished the whole survey in two weeks.
examples.cn: 我们用两周完成了整项调查。

examples.en: She accomplished her aim without raising her voice.
examples.cn: 她没有提高嗓门就实现了目的。

examples.en: Little was accomplished at the meeting.
examples.cn: 会上几乎没办成什么事。

dict_mnemonic.text: ac-（向）+ compl（填满）+ -ish（动词）= 把事填满 → 完成

root: 拉丁语 complere（填满）加 ad-（朝向）→ 古法语 acomplir；同族词有 accomplishment、accomplished、complete、supply。

sensesIntro.en: Accomplish always means reaching the end of a piece of work, whether the work is a task, a goal or a life.
sensesIntro.cn: accomplish 始终指走到一件工作的尽头，无论这件工作是任务、目标还是一生。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the last item on a list crossed out.
core.cn: 核心意象：清单最后一项被划掉。

branches.en: TASK LINE: the work is brought to its end.
branches.cn: 任务线：工作做到终点。

branches.en: GOAL LINE: the aim held in advance is reached.
branches.cn: 目标线：事先握住的终点被抵达。

branches.en: RECORD LINE: the result earns mention.
branches.cn: 成绩线：结果值得被提起。

branches.en: CONTRAST: to attempt is to start, to accomplish is to arrive.
branches.cn: 对照线：attempt 是开始，accomplish 是抵达。

branches.en: WORTH LINE: the verb can measure value, not only endings.
branches.cn: 价值线：这个动词也衡量价值，不只看结束。

intro.en: A prefix of direction on a Latin root of filling, carried through a French verb.
intro.cn: 一个表方向的前缀加拉丁「填满」词根，经法语动词传来。

latinIntro.en: Com- plus plere gave complere, to fill up, and Old French turned it into acomplir.
latinIntro.cn: com- 加 plere 得 complere「填满」，古法语把它变为 acomplir。

items.example: It points the filling at a task.
items.exampleCN: 它把「填满」指向一项任务。
它也出现在 complete 里。

definition_en: a state of agreement, or a formal arrangement between parties
core_image: 两张纸并排放在桌上，折痕与字句都对得整整齐齐
scene: 谈判到深夜，两边终于在文件上签了字。The two reports are in accord on the main point.
sceneCN: 这里 accord 是「一致」（第 1 个义项：彼此相合）；句意是两份报告在主要问题上是一致的。

pos.zh: 名词：一致；符合；协议
动词：与…一致；给予

senses.title: A state of agreement
senses.titleCN: 一致：彼此相合
senses.definition: a condition in which things fit together
senses.definitionCN: 几样事物彼此吻合的状态
senses.example: His story is in accord with hers.
senses.exampleCN: 他的说法与她的相符。
senses.why: Latin cor means heart; accord is hearts brought to the same place.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 cor 意为「心」，accord 就是心被带到同一处。

senses.title: One's own wish
senses.titleCN: 自愿：出于本人意愿
senses.definition: of one's own free will
senses.definitionCN: 出于自己不受强迫的意愿
senses.example: She left of her own accord.
senses.exampleCN: 她是自愿离开的。
senses.why: Two hearts agreeing also describes one heart not being pushed.
senses.whyCN: 两心相合也可以描述一颗心没有被推动。

senses.title: A formal agreement
senses.titleCN: 协议：正式达成的约定
senses.definition: a treaty or arrangement between parties
senses.definitionCN: 各方正式达成的条约或安排
senses.example: The two countries signed a trade accord.
senses.exampleCN: 两国签署了一项贸易协定。
senses.why: Set the agreement on paper and the noun becomes a document.
senses.whyCN: 把这种一致落到纸上，这个名词就成了文件。

senses.title: To grant something
senses.titleCN: 给予：正式授予
senses.definition: to give something such as honour or rights
senses.definitionCN: 给予荣誉或权利等
senses.example: The hall accords great honour to its founders.
senses.exampleCN: 这座礼堂给予创建者很高的荣誉。
senses.why: Latin accordare meant to bring hearts together, and granting is one way to do it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 accordare 意为「使心相合」，授予正是使之相合的一种方式。

intro.en: Accord comes from Latin accordare, from ad- plus cor, heart, to bring hearts together.
intro.cn: accord 来自拉丁语 accordare，由 ad- 加 cor「心」构成，意为「使心相合」。

items.en: Cor meant heart, and it underlies cordial, courage and record.
items.cn: cor 意为「心」，也是 cordial、courage 与 record 的底层词。

items.en: Accordare meant to bring hearts into harmony.
items.cn: accordare 意为「使心归于和谐」。

items.en: Old French acorder meant to reconcile and to agree.
items.cn: 古法语 acorder 意为「调和、同意」。

items.en: English accord covered being of one mind and giving what is due.
items.cn: 英语 accord 兼指同心与给予应得之物。

items.en: The noun also names treaties between states.
items.cn: 这个名词也用来指国家间的条约。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the cord- heart root; the near-meaning group holds words of agreement.
note.cn: 形近组共用 cord-「心」词根；近义组收表示一致的词。

entries.definition: Agreement, mostly in the phrase in accordance with.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「一致」，多用于 in accordance with。

entries.definition: Therefore, or in a matching way.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「因此、相应地」。

entries.definition: A folded instrument; it looks close but is unrelated in use.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「手风琴」，形近而用法无关。

entries.definition: The plain word for being of one mind.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「同意、协议」，最常用。

entries.definition: A pleasing fit between parts, warmer than accord.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「和谐」，比 accord 更温暖。

entries.definition: A formal written agreement between states.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「条约」，更正式。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the heart root, the own-accord phrase and the peace accord.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借「心」词根、of one's own accord 与和平协议。

normal.en: Cor is heart, so accord means hearts standing in the same place.
normal.cn: cor 是心，因此 accord 意为几颗心站在同一处。

normal.en: Cordial and courage share the same heart root with accord.
normal.cn: cordial 与 courage 和 accord 共用同一个「心」词根。

normal.en: Of one's own accord is the phrase that means nobody pushed you.
normal.cn: of one's own accord 这个短语意思是没人推你。

normal.en: In accord with is the formal cousin of the everyday agreeing with.
normal.cn: in accord with 是日常 agreeing with 的正式近亲。

normal.en: A peace accord is an agreement that has been signed and filmed.
normal.cn: a peace accord 是一份被签下并被拍进镜头的协议。

abstract.en: Agreement between minds is pictured as agreement between hearts, and the picture is older than the law.
abstract.cn: 心智的一致被画成心脏的一致，这幅画比法律更古老。

abstract.en: To give what is due is also to fit two sides together, so granting and agreeing are one word.
abstract.cn: 给予应得之物也是把两边配到一起，于是授予与一致成了同一个词。

abstract.en: A treaty is accord frozen on paper, still carrying the warm root under the seal.
abstract.cn: 条约是被冻在纸上的 accord，封蜡下面仍带着那枚温暖的词根。

examples.en: What he said is in accord with the written record.
examples.cn: 他所说的与书面记录一致。

examples.en: The two sides reached an accord after long talks.
examples.cn: 经过长时间谈判，双方达成了协议。

examples.en: No one told him to leave; he went of his own accord.
examples.cn: 没人要他走，他是自愿离开的。

dict_mnemonic.text: ac-（向）+ cord（心）= 心朝一处 → 一致

root: 拉丁语 cor（心）加 ad-（朝向）→ accordare（使心相合）；同族词有 accordance、accordingly、cordial、courage、record、concord。

sensesIntro.en: Accord begins with two hearts and ends on a signed page, with a stop along the way for one willing heart.
sensesIntro.cn: accord 从两颗心开始，落到签好的纸页，中途还停下来讲了讲一颗情愿的心。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two sheets lying side by side, folds matching.
core.cn: 核心意象：两张纸并排放着，折痕对得上。

branches.en: FIT LINE: the accounts match.
branches.cn: 吻合线：说法彼此相符。

branches.en: WILL LINE: no one is pushing the person.
branches.cn: 意愿线：没有人推着这个人。

branches.en: PAPER LINE: the match is signed as a treaty.
branches.cn: 纸面线：这种吻合被签成条约。

branches.en: GIFT LINE: honour is granted to someone.
branches.cn: 给予线：荣誉被授予某人。

branches.en: CONTRAST: disagreement splits the hearts, accord puts them back.
branches.cn: 对照线：分歧把心分开，accord 把它们放回一处。

intro.en: A prefix of direction on the Latin word for heart.
intro.cn: 一个表方向的前缀加拉丁语里「心」这个词。

latinIntro.en: Ad- plus cor produced accordare, to bring hearts together.
latinIntro.cn: ad- 加 cor 得 accordare，即「使心相合」。

items.exampleCN: 它也出现在 courage 里。

definition_en: the state of agreeing with something, used mostly in set phrases
core_image: 一份文件上的条款，与桌上另一份旧规定逐条对得上
scene: 公司在处理这件事时，完全按着合同条款来办。The work was done in accordance with the agreement.
sceneCN: 这里 accordance 是「依照」（第 1 个义项：与某规定一致并据此行事）；句意是这项工作是按协议进行的。

pos.zh: 名词：一致；符合；依照

senses.title: Agreeing with a rule
senses.titleCN: 符合：与规定相符
senses.definition: the state of matching a rule or standard
senses.definitionCN: 与规则或标准相吻合的状态
senses.example: The building was built in accordance with the code.
senses.exampleCN: 这座建筑是按规范建造的。
senses.why: The noun never stands alone in modern use; it lives inside in accordance with.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词在现代英语里从不单独站立，它住在 in accordance with 里面。

senses.title: Followed as a guide
senses.titleCN: 依照：把某物当作行动依据
senses.definition: following something as a guide for action
senses.definitionCN: 以某物作为行动的依据
senses.example: Act in accordance with your own judgement.
senses.exampleCN: 按你自己的判断行事。
senses.why: Matching a rule and following it are the same act seen from two sides.
senses.whyCN: 符合规则与遵循规则是同一动作的两面。

senses.title: A formal fit between texts
senses.titleCN: 吻合：文本之间的对应
senses.definition: a formal correspondence between two documents
senses.definitionCN: 两份文件之间的正式对应
senses.example: The report is in accordance with the audit.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告与审计结果相符。
senses.why: When two papers fit line by line, the abstract fit becomes visible on the page.
senses.whyCN: 当两份文件逐行相合，抽象的一致就变得纸面上看得见。

intro.en: Accordance joins accord, from Latin ad- plus cor, heart, with the Latin noun ending -antia.
intro.cn: accordance 由 accord（拉丁语 ad- 加 cor「心」）加名词词尾 -antia 构成。

items.en: Cor meant heart, and accordare meant to bring hearts together.
items.cn: cor 意为「心」，accordare 意为「使心相合」。

items.en: Old French acorder gave English the verb and the noun.
items.cn: 古法语 acorder 给英语带来了动词与名词。

items.en: Accordantia named the state of being in harmony.
items.cn: accordantia 指处于和谐中的状态。

items.en: English accordance meant agreement of things or persons.
items.cn: 英语 accordance 指事物或人的相互一致。

items.en: The noun now survives almost entirely in in accordance with.
items.cn: 这个名词如今几乎只存于 in accordance with 中。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the accord family; the near-meaning group holds words of conforming.
note.cn: 形近组共用 accord 家族；近义组收表示遵照的词。

entries.definition: Therefore, or in a matching manner.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「因此、相应地」。

entries.definition: The noun and verb behind this form.
entries.definitionCN: 名词与动词，义为「一致、协议」。

entries.definition: A folded musical instrument, unrelated in use.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「手风琴」，形近而用法无关。

entries.definition: Obeying a rule, a stronger word than accordance.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「遵守」，比 accordance 更强。

entries.definition: Matching an accepted standard.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「符合」，偏标准。

entries.definition: The plain word for fitting together.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「一致」，最朴素。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the fixed phrase, the heart root and the -ance noun ending.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借固定短语、「心」词根与 -ance 名词词尾。

normal.en: Accordance almost always arrives inside in accordance with, like a word with a fixed seat.
normal.cn: accordance 几乎总坐在 in accordance with 里，像个有固定座位的词。

normal.en: Drop the -ance and you get accord, still carrying the heart root.
normal.cn: 去掉 -ance 就是 accord，仍带着「心」的词根。

normal.en: In accordance with the law is the coldest, most official version of the phrase.
normal.cn: in accordance with the law 是这个短语最冷、最公文的说法。

normal.en: Accordance is the noun; accordingly is the adverb that follows from it.
normal.cn: accordance 是名词，accordingly 是由它而来的副词。

normal.en: A building permit is a paper that asks for accordance, not for opinion.
normal.cn: 建筑许可证是一张要求「符合」而非意见的纸。

abstract.en: Accordance is agreement stripped of warmth, kept only as a standard for judging.
abstract.cn: accordance 是被剥去温度的一致，只作为评判标准保留下来。

abstract.en: A rule exists so that action and text can be compared from a distance.
abstract.cn: 规则的存在，是为了让行动与文本能隔着距离相互比对。

abstract.en: The word is a hinge, joining what was written to what is done.
abstract.cn: 这个词是一枚折页，把写下的与做出的连在一起。

examples.en: Payment must be made in accordance with the contract.
examples.cn: 付款必须按照合同进行。

examples.en: The factory now operates in accordance with the new rules.
examples.cn: 这家工厂现在按新规定运营。

examples.en: The results were in accordance with our expectations.
examples.cn: 结果与我们的预期相符。

dict_mnemonic.text: accord（一致）+ -ance（名词）= 一致的状态，多用于「依照」

root: 拉丁语 cor（心）加 ad- → accordare（使相合），名词 accordantia；同族词有 accord、accordingly、according to。

sensesIntro.en: Accordance names agreement only as a yardstick, and so it almost always comes with a rule or a document.
sensesIntro.cn: accordance 只把一致当作一把尺，因此几乎总和规则或文件一起出现。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: clauses on one page matched to clauses on another.
core.cn: 核心意象：一页条款对上另一页条款。

branches.en: RULE LINE: the thing fits a written standard.
branches.cn: 规则线：事物符合书面标准。

branches.en: GUIDE LINE: the standard is followed in action.
branches.cn: 指引线：行动照着标准走。

branches.en: TEXT LINE: two documents line up.
branches.cn: 文本线：两份文件逐条对齐。

branches.en: CONTRAST: accordance is checked; agreement is felt.
branches.cn: 对照线：accordance 被查验，agreement 被感受。

branches.en: TONE LINE: the phrase belongs to forms and contracts.
branches.cn: 语气线：这个短语属于表格与合同。

intro.en: The accord family with a Latin noun ending that names a state.
intro.cn: accord 家族加上一个命名状态的名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Accordantia, from accordare, named the state of hearts being together, and English narrowed it.
latinIntro.cn: 源自 accordare 的 accordantia 指心意相合的状态，英语把它收窄了。

items.example: It draws two things toward fit.
items.exampleCN: 它把两样东西拉向吻合。
它也出现在 cordial 里。

definition_en: in a way that matches what has just been said, or for that reason
core_image: 一句话说完，下一句话立刻跟着它拐了个方向
