scene: 客人比预定时间早到了两个小时，厨房只好临时把出菜顺序全部提前。Prices rose, and the budget was adjusted accordingly.
sceneCN: 这里 accordingly 是「相应地」（第 1 个义项：与前文所述情况相吻合地）；句意是价格上涨，预算也相应作了调整。

pos.zh: 副词：因此；相应地；照着

senses.title: In a matching way
senses.titleCN: 相应地：与前文情况相吻合
senses.definition: in a way that suits what has been said
senses.definitionCN: 以符合前面所述情况的方式
senses.example: The rules changed, so the forms were redesigned accordingly.
senses.exampleCN: 规定变了，表格也随之重新设计。
senses.why: The -ly adverb says the second act takes the shape of the first.
senses.whyCN: -ly 副词表示第二个动作照着第一个的形状去做。

senses.title: For that reason
senses.titleCN: 因此：作为结果
senses.definition: as a result of what has just been said
senses.definitionCN: 作为刚说过的事情的结果
senses.example: He was late, and accordingly missed the start.
senses.exampleCN: 他迟到了，因此错过了开场。
senses.why: Matching can harden into consequence when the first fact leaves no choice.
senses.whyCN: 当第一个事实没有留下余地时，这种吻合就硬化成了结果。

senses.title: As stated by
senses.titleCN: 根据：依照所引内容
senses.definition: as said or shown by a source
senses.definitionCN: 依照某个来源所说或所示
senses.example: The weather, according to the forecast, will turn cold.
senses.exampleCN: 根据预报，天气会转冷。
senses.why: The related phrase according to points back at a source rather than at a result.
senses.whyCN: 相关短语 according to 指回一个来源，而不是指向结果。

intro.en: Accordingly is according plus -ly, from accord, Latin ad- plus cor, heart.
intro.cn: accordingly 是 according 加 -ly，源自 accord，即拉丁语 ad- 加 cor「心」。

items.en: Cor meant heart, and accordare meant to bring hearts together.
items.cn: cor 意为「心」，accordare 意为「使心相合」。

items.en: Old French acorder gave English accord with its sense of fitting.
items.cn: 古法语 acorder 给英语 accord 带来了「相合」之义。

items.en: According first meant matching or in agreement with.
items.cn: according 起初意为「与…相符」。

items.en: The adverb accordingly grew to mark a consequence.
items.cn: 副词 accordingly 逐渐用来标记结果。

items.en: Official writing uses it constantly for matching action to rule.
items.cn: 公文写作大量用它表示行动与规定相配。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the accord family; the near-meaning group holds words of consequence.
note.cn: 形近组共用 accord 家族；近义组收表示结果的词。

entries.definition: Agreement, as in in accordance with.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「一致」，见于 in accordance with。

entries.definition: Agreement between parties.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「一致、协议」。

entries.definition: As stated by a source.
entries.definitionCN: 短语，义为「根据」，指向来源。

entries.definition: For that reason, a plainer word.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「因此」，更朴素。

entries.definition: As a result, more formal than therefore.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「结果」，比 therefore 更正式。

entries.definition: In a way that matches a first change.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「相应地」，偏对应关系。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the accordingly-as-result sense and the official-writing tone.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借 accordingly 表结果的义项与公文语气。

normal.en: Accordingly sits at the head of a sentence that answers the one before it.
normal.cn: accordingly 坐在一句回答前一句的话的开头。

normal.en: Adjust accordingly is the most common two-word ending in reports.
normal.cn: adjust accordingly 是报告里最常见的两词结尾。

normal.en: According to points at a source; accordingly points at a consequence.
normal.cn: according to 指向来源，accordingly 指向结果。

normal.en: The heart root hides under the -ly, and the adverb sounds like pure logic.
normal.cn: -ly 下面藏着「心」的词根，而这个副词听起来像纯粹的逻辑。

normal.en: Therefore says why; accordingly says how to match.
normal.cn: therefore 说的是为什么，accordingly 说的是该怎么对上。

abstract.en: The adverb is a hand pointing back over the shoulder at the reason just given.
abstract.cn: 这个副词是一只手，向肩后指着刚给出的理由。

abstract.en: Matching and consequence are close: if one thing changes, the other has little choice.
abstract.cn: 吻合与结果靠得很近：一件变了，另一件也难得选择。

abstract.en: Official prose leans on it because it lets action follow rule without argument.
abstract.cn: 公文倚重它，因为它让行动不必争论就跟着规则走。

examples.en: The deadline moved, so we planned accordingly.
examples.cn: 截止日期改了，所以我们也相应改了计划。

examples.en: He knew the risks and acted accordingly.
examples.cn: 他知道风险，也据此采取行动。

examples.en: Prices fell; accordingly, demand rose.
examples.cn: 价格下降，因此需求上升。

dict_mnemonic.text: according（相符）+ -ly（副词）= 照着前面的情况来 → 相应地

root: accord（拉丁语 cor「心」+ ad-，意为「相合」）+ -ing + -ly；同族词有 accordance、according to。

sensesIntro.en: Accordingly always ties a second statement to a first, whether as a matching shape or as a plain consequence.
sensesIntro.cn: accordingly 总把第二句话系在第一句上，或以相配的形状，或以直白的结果。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sentence turning the moment the one before it ends.
core.cn: 核心意象：一句话刚说完，下一句立刻转向。

branches.en: MATCH LINE: the response copies the change.
branches.cn: 对应线：回应照着变化走。

branches.en: RESULT LINE: the change forces the next step.
branches.cn: 结果线：变化逼出下一步。

branches.en: SOURCE LINE: according to names where the claim came from.
branches.cn: 来源线：according to 指明说法出处。

branches.en: CONTRAST: therefore explains, accordingly instructs.
branches.cn: 对照线：therefore 解释，accordingly 指示。

branches.en: TONE LINE: the adverb belongs to memos and reports.
branches.cn: 语气线：这个副词属于备忘与报告。

intro.en: The accord family with two endings that turn it into an adverb of matching.
intro.cn: accord 家族加上两个词尾，把它变成表「相配」的副词。

latinIntro.en: From ad- plus cor, the verb accord led to according, and the adverb followed in English.
latinIntro.cn: 由 ad- 加 cor 构成的 accord 派生出 according，副词随后在英语中出现。

definition_zh: 账户；账目；描述；解释；重要
definition_en: a record of money held somewhere, or a report of what happened
core_image: 一本账簿摊在桌上，一行行数字与一行行说明并排
scene: 月底对账时，出纳把每一笔进出都念了一遍。He gave a clear account of the whole evening.
sceneCN: 这里 account 是「描述」（第 3 个义项：对事件的叙述）；句意是他把整个晚上清楚地讲了一遍。

pos.zh: 名词：账户；账目；描述；解释
动词：解释；说明；占（比例）

senses.title: A record of money
senses.titleCN: 账户：记录钱款的地方
senses.definition: an arrangement for keeping money with a bank or shop
senses.definitionCN: 在银行或商店保存钱款的安排
senses.example: She opened a savings account at eighteen.
senses.exampleCN: 她十八岁时开了个储蓄账户。
senses.why: Latin computare meant to reckon, and a record of money is a reckoning kept in one place.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 computare 意为「计算」，钱的记录就是收在一处的清算。

senses.title: A statement of debts
senses.titleCN: 账目：应付款项的清单
senses.definition: a bill or a record of what is owed
senses.definitionCN: 应付账款的清单或单据
senses.example: Settle the account before you leave.
senses.exampleCN: 离开前把账结掉。
senses.why: The same reckoning can be turned toward a person and become a demand.
senses.whyCN: 同一份清算可以转向某个人，变成一份催讨。

senses.title: A description of events
senses.titleCN: 描述：对事情的叙述
senses.definition: a report of what happened, spoken or written
senses.definitionCN: 对发生之事的口头或书面讲述
senses.example: The witness gave a full account of the crash.
senses.exampleCN: 目击者完整讲述了这场撞车。
senses.why: To give an account is to render the reckoning of events in words.
senses.whyCN: give an account 就是用言语交代事件的那份清算。

senses.title: To explain or to make up
senses.titleCN: 解释或占比：说明原因或构成比例
senses.definition: to explain a cause, or to form a part of a total
senses.definitionCN: 说明某个原因，或构成总量中的一部分
senses.example: How do you account for the missing files?
senses.exampleCN: 那些丢失的文件你怎么解释？
senses.why: Neither the money nor the story is present here, only the settling of a question.
senses.whyCN: 此处既没有钱也没有故事，只有对一个疑问的清算。

intro.en: Account comes from Old French acont, from Latin computare, to reckon together.
intro.cn: account 来自古法语 acont，上溯拉丁语 computare「一同计算」。

items.en: Putare meant to think or to reckon, and it underlies compute and reputation.
items.cn: putare 意为「思考、计算」，也是 compute 与 reputation 的底层词。

items.en: Computare meant to reckon things together, especially money.
items.cn: computare 意为「把事物算在一起」，尤指钱。

items.en: Acont named a reckoning or a settlement of money.
items.cn: acont 指清算或钱款的结清。

items.en: English account covered money records and, from the 1600s, narratives.
items.cn: 英语 account 先指钱的记录，17 世纪起也指叙述。

items.en: The word now spans banking, reporting, explanation and share.
items.cn: 这个词如今横跨银行、叙述、解释与占比。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the account family; the near-meaning group holds words of records and reports.
note.cn: 形近组共用 account 家族；近义组收记录与叙述类的词。

entries.definition: A person who keeps and checks accounts.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「会计」。

entries.definition: Required to explain and answer for acts.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「负有责任的」。

entries.definition: A total quantity; the letters differ at the end.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「数量」，词尾不同。

entries.definition: A formal statement of facts, close to the third sense.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「报告」，接近第三义项。

entries.definition: A written demand for payment.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「账单」，接近第二义项。

entries.definition: The verb for making a cause clear.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「解释」，对应第四义项。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the reckon root, the account for phrase and the accountant cousin.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借「计算」词根、account for 短语与 accountant 这个近亲。

normal.en: Account shares a root with compute: both are about reckoning.
normal.cn: account 与 compute 同根：两者都关于计算。

normal.en: Take into account means putting a factor into the sum before deciding.
normal.cn: take into account 意思是在下决定前把一个因素计入总数。

normal.en: Account for does double duty: explain a cause, or make up a share.
normal.cn: account for 有两用：解释原因，或占据一份。

normal.en: An accountant is a person whose whole work is the account.
normal.cn: accountant 就是整个工作都围绕 account 的人。

normal.en: On account of is a formal way of saying because.
normal.cn: on account of 是 because 的正式说法。

abstract.en: A reckoning of money and a reckoning of events use the same word, because both settle a question.
abstract.cn: 对钱的清算与对事件的清算用同一个词，因为两者都在结一个问题。

abstract.en: To be accountable is to know that someone will one day add up what you did.
abstract.cn: 负责任的含意是知道有一天会有人把你做的加起来。

abstract.en: The word keeps a straight column: what came in, what went out, what remains.
abstract.cn: 这个词始终有一条直的栏目：进来什么，出去什么，剩下什么。

examples.en: Please pay this bill into my account.
examples.cn: 请把这笔钱付到我的账户上。

examples.en: We must take the weather into account.
examples.cn: 我们必须把天气考虑进去。

examples.en: She gave a moving account of her childhood.
examples.cn: 她动情地讲述了她的童年。

dict_mnemonic.text: ac-（向）+ count（数）= 把钱数清楚 → 账户、账目

root: 拉丁语 computare（计算）经古法语 acont 进入英语；同族词有 accountant、accounting、accountable、compute、count。

sensesIntro.en: Account keeps one habit in every sense: it adds something up, whether money, debts, events or reasons.
sensesIntro.cn: account 在每个义项里都保持同一个习惯：把某样东西加起来，无论是钱、债、事件还是原因。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ledger where numbers and notes stand in parallel lines.
core.cn: 核心意象：账簿上数字与说明并排。

branches.en: BANK LINE: money is held and counted.
branches.cn: 银行线：钱被存放并计点。

branches.en: DEBT LINE: the reckoning becomes a bill.
branches.cn: 债务线：清算变成一张账单。

branches.en: STORY LINE: events are reckoned in words.
branches.cn: 叙述线：事件用言语清算。

branches.en: REASON LINE: a cause is settled or a share is counted.
branches.cn: 原因线：原因被交代，或份额被计入。

branches.en: CONTRAST: a report states, an account settles.
branches.cn: 对照线：report 陈述，account 交代。

intro.en: A prefix of direction with the Latin root of reckoning, worn down by French.
intro.cn: 一个表方向的前缀加拉丁「计算」词根，经法语磨损而成。

latinIntro.en: Computare, to reckon together, became Old French acont and then English account.
latinIntro.cn: computare「一同计算」变为古法语 acont，再成为英语 account。

items.example: It points the reckoning at a sum.
items.exampleCN: 它把计算指向一个总数。

items.example: It is the bare verb inside the word.

definition_en: the condition of being required to explain and answer for what one does
core_image: 一张公开的桌子，一头坐着提问的人，一头坐着必须回答的人
scene: 事故调查结束后，报告的第一条建议是建立明确的责任制度。Public accountability was the main demand of the protesters.
sceneCN: 这里 accountability 是「问责制」（第 1 个义项：必须为行为作出交代的制度）；句意是公众问责是抗议者的主要诉求。

pos.zh: 名词：责任；问责制；可追究性

senses.title: The duty to answer
senses.titleCN: 责任：必须作出交代的义务
senses.definition: the obligation to explain one's acts to those with a right to ask
senses.definitionCN: 向有权追问者解释自身行为的义务
senses.example: Ministers accepted accountability for the failures.
senses.exampleCN: 部长们承认对这些失败负有责任。
senses.why: The -ity ending names a condition, so the word is about a state one can be held in.
senses.whyCN: -ity 词尾命名一种状态，因此这个词讲的是一个人可被置于其中的处境。

senses.title: A system of checking power
senses.titleCN: 问责制：约束权力的制度
senses.definition: the set of rules by which power is questioned and judged
senses.definitionCN: 追问与评判权力的一套规则
senses.example: The new law created accountability for police spending.
senses.exampleCN: 新法律为警方开支设立了问责机制。
senses.why: A single duty can be built into institutions, and then the noun means the machinery.
senses.whyCN: 单一的义务可以被建成制度，此时这个名词指的是一套机器。

senses.title: Being explainable and open
senses.titleCN: 可追究性：经得起公开审查
senses.definition: the quality of being open to public scrutiny
senses.definitionCN: 经得起公众审查的性质
senses.example: Solar panels bring accountability to household energy use.
senses.exampleCN: 太阳能板让家庭用电变得可被核查。
senses.why: When nothing is hidden, the word shifts from blame to openness.
senses.whyCN: 当没有任何东西被藏起时，这个词就从责难转向公开。

intro.en: Accountability is accountable plus -ity, from account, Latin computare, to reckon.
intro.cn: accountability 是 accountable 加 -ity，源自 account，即拉丁语 computare「计算」。

items.en: Computare meant to reckon together, the base of the account family.
items.cn: computare 意为「一同计算」，是 account 家族的基础。

items.en: Acont named the reckoning of money owed and paid.
items.cn: acont 指对欠付与已付钱款的清算。

items.en: Accountable first meant required to render a sum.
items.cn: accountable 起初指须交代一笔款项。

items.en: Accountability grew with public budgets and company law.
items.cn: accountability 随公共预算与公司法一同壮大。

items.en: The word is now central to government and business ethics.
items.cn: 这个词如今是政府与商业伦理的核心词。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the accountable family; the near-meaning group holds words of responsibility.
note.cn: 形近组共用 accountable 家族；近义组收表示责任的词。

entries.definition: Required to answer for what one does.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「负有责任的」。

entries.definition: A keeper of financial records, a different job.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「会计」，同族但所指不同。

entries.definition: The profession of keeping accounts.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「会计行业」，形近而义异。

entries.definition: Being in charge of something, wider in scope.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「责任」，范围更宽。

entries.definition: Openness about decisions and money.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「透明度」，接近第三义项。

entries.definition: Legal responsibility for cost or harm.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「法律责任」，偏法律。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the -ity ending, the public-table picture and the pair with transparency.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借 -ity 词尾、公开桌子的画面，以及与 transparency 的搭配。

normal.en: Accountability is accountable turned into a noun you can demand.
normal.cn: accountability 是把 accountable 变成可以要求的名词。

normal.en: Demand accountability is the phrase shouted at the end of a scandal.
normal.cn: demand accountability 是丑闻尾声时被喊出的短语。

normal.en: Transparency and accountability travel together: one shows, one answers.
normal.cn: transparency 与 accountability 同行：一个展示，一个作答。

normal.en: The -ity ending makes a state, while -ant would have made a person.
normal.cn: -ity 词尾造出状态，而 -ant 本会造出一个人。

normal.en: Accountability adds -ability to account, so the word is about being called to answer.
normal.cn: accountability 是在 account 上加 -ability，因此这个词讲的是被叫去作答。

abstract.en: Power that cannot be questioned quietly stops being borrowed and starts being owned.
abstract.cn: 无法被追问的权力，会悄悄从「借用」变成「占有」。

abstract.en: Accountability is trust with a receipt attached.
abstract.cn: 问责是附了收据的信任。

abstract.en: The word assumes two parties and a record between them, which is why it needs writing.
abstract.cn: 这个词预设了两方以及它们之间的一份记录，因此它需要书写。

examples.en: The report called for greater accountability in local government.
examples.cn: 报告呼吁地方政府加强问责。

examples.en: There is no accountability when no one keeps records.
examples.cn: 没有人记录时，就谈不上问责。

examples.en: Voters demanded accountability for the wasted funds.
examples.cn: 选民要求对浪费的资金追究责任。

dict_mnemonic.text: account（算账）+ -able（可…的）+ -ity（名词）= 可被要求算账的状态 → 问责

root: account（拉丁语 computare「计算」）+ -able + -ity（名词词尾）；同族词有 accountable、accountably、accountant。

sensesIntro.en: Accountability names a duty, then the institutions built to enforce it, then the openness that makes it possible.
sensesIntro.cn: accountability 先命名一项义务，再命名执行它的制度，最后命名使它可能的公开。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two chairs facing each other across a public table.
core.cn: 核心意象：公开的桌子两边对坐两只椅子。

branches.en: DUTY LINE: a person owes an explanation.
branches.cn: 义务线：一个人欠着一份解释。

branches.en: SYSTEM LINE: rules question and judge power.
branches.cn: 制度线：规则追问并评判权力。

branches.en: OPENNESS LINE: records let anyone check.
branches.cn: 公开线：记录让人人都能核查。

branches.en: CONTRAST: responsibility spreads, accountability is enforced.
branches.cn: 对照线：responsibility 铺开，accountability 被强制执行。

branches.en: TONE LINE: the word belongs to politics, law and audits.
branches.cn: 语气线：这个词属于政治、法律与审计。

intro.en: The account family with two endings that make a state of being answerable.
intro.cn: account 家族加两个词尾，构成一种「须作交代」的状态。

latinIntro.en: Computare became account, then accountable, then accountability, each ending adding a layer.
latinIntro.cn: computare 成为 account，再成 accountable，再成 accountability，每个词尾都加了一层。

items.example: It marks what can be demanded.
items.exampleCN: 它标记可被要求的东西。

items.example: It forms the noun of state.

definition_zh: 负有责任的；须作解释的
definition_en: required to explain your actions to someone who has the right to ask
core_image: 一个人站在桌前，被问一句「为什么要这样做」，必须开口回答
scene: 项目出了纰漏，负责人被要求到会议上说明每一步的决定。Managers are accountable to the board for every payment.
sceneCN: 这里 accountable 是「负有责任的」（第 1 个义项：须为行为作出交代）；句意是经理们须就每一笔付款向董事会负责。

pos.zh: 形容词：负有责任的；须作解释的

derivatives.zh: 义为「无法解释的、不受问责的」

senses.title: Answerable to someone
senses.titleCN: 负有责任：须向某人交代
senses.definition: required to answer for your conduct to another
senses.definitionCN: 须就自己的行为向他人作出交代
senses.example: The minister is accountable to parliament.
senses.exampleCN: 部长须向议会负责。
senses.why: The -able ending means able to be called to account, and the calling presupposes someone above.
senses.whyCN: -able 词尾意为「可被要求交代」，而要求交代的前提是上面有人。

senses.title: Answerable for a duty
senses.titleCN: 对职责负责：为某项事务担责
senses.definition: responsible for a task or a sum entrusted to you
senses.definitionCN: 为自己受托的任务或款项负责
senses.example: Each officer is accountable for the equipment issued.
senses.exampleCN: 每位警官对所配发的装备负责。
senses.why: The thing answered for can be an act or an object, and here it is an object held in trust.
senses.whyCN: 需要交代的可以是一个行为，也可以是一件物品，此处是受托保管的物品。

senses.title: Open to explanation
senses.titleCN: 可被说明的：经得起追问
senses.definition: able to be explained and justified when questioned
senses.definitionCN: 在被追问时能说明并辩护
senses.example: Every decision must be accountable to the public.
senses.exampleCN: 每个决定都必须经得起公众的追问。
senses.why: When the answer comes easily, the word turns from burden into a standard.
senses.whyCN: 当答案来得容易时，这个词就从负担变成一条标准。

intro.en: Accountable is account plus -able, from Latin computare, to reckon, meaning able to be called to account.
intro.cn: accountable 是 account 加 -able，源自拉丁语 computare「计算」，意为「可以被要求交代的」。

items.en: Computare meant to reckon together, the root of account.
items.cn: computare 意为「一同计算」，是 account 的词根。

items.en: Acont named a reckoning of money owed or received.
items.cn: acont 指对欠付或收取钱款的清算。

items.en: English used accountable for sums a person had to render.
items.cn: 英语早期用 accountable 指须交代的款项。

items.en: The word widened from money to conduct and office.
items.cn: 这个词从钱款扩展到行为与职务。

items.en: Accountability became a central word of public life.
items.cn: accountability 成了公共生活中的核心词。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the account family; the near-meaning group holds words of responsibility.
note.cn: 形近组共用 account 家族；近义组收表示责任的词。

entries.definition: The duty of being called to account.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「问责、责任」。

entries.definition: A person who keeps financial accounts.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「会计」，同族不同义。

entries.definition: A record or an explanation.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「账户、解释」。

entries.definition: In charge of something and answerable for it.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有责任的」，最常用。

entries.definition: Legally bound for cost or damage.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「负有法律责任的」，偏法律。

entries.definition: Required to reply for what one did.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「须作交代的」，最贴字面。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the called-to-account picture and the to and for pair.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借「被叫去交代」的画面，以及 to 与 for 的搭配分工。

normal.en: Accountable means able to be called to account, and the caller is above you.
normal.cn: accountable 意为「可被叫去交代」，叫你的人在你上面。

normal.en: Accountable to a person, accountable for a thing: the two prepositions split the job.
normal.cn: accountable to 接人，accountable for 接事：两个介词分好了工。

normal.en: Hold someone accountable is the phrase used after a failure.
normal.cn: hold someone accountable 是失败之后用的短语。

normal.en: Accountability is the noun that turns the adjective into a system.
normal.cn: accountability 是把形容词变成一套制度的名词。

normal.en: Unaccountable means either not explainable or not answerable to anyone.
normal.cn: unaccountable 既指「无法解释」，也指「不受任何人问责」。

abstract.en: Power without a person above it has nowhere to render an account.
abstract.cn: 没有谁在其上，权力便无处交代账目。

abstract.en: To be accountable is to accept that your reasons will one day be read aloud.
abstract.cn: 负责任就是接受有一天你的理由会被当众念出来。

abstract.en: The word is a table with two chairs: one who asks and one who answers.
abstract.cn: 这个词是一张有两只椅子的桌子：一只问，一只答。

examples.en: Managers are accountable for the decisions they make.
examples.cn: 经理们要为自己作出的决定负责。

examples.en: The agency is accountable to the public through parliament.
examples.cn: 这个机构通过议会向公众负责。

examples.en: Someone must be held accountable for the failure.
examples.cn: 必须有人为这次失败承担责任。

dict_mnemonic.text: account（算账）+ -able（可…的）= 可以被叫来算账的 → 负有责任

root: account（拉丁语 computare「计算」）+ -able（可…的）；同族词有 accountability、accountant、account。

sensesIntro.en: Accountable always puts two people in the room: one who must explain and one who may ask.
sensesIntro.cn: accountable 总是把两个人放进同一个房间：一个必须解释，一个可以发问。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person standing to answer a single question.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人站着回答一句追问。

branches.en: PERSON LINE: an answer is owed to someone above.
branches.cn: 人对线：须向上级交代。

branches.en: THING LINE: a task or a sum is held in trust.
branches.cn: 事物线：任务或款项被受托保管。

branches.en: STANDARD LINE: any decision must bear questioning.
branches.cn: 标准线：任何决定都须经得起追问。

branches.en: CONTRAST: responsible is broader, accountable names the reckoning.
branches.cn: 对照线：responsible 更宽，accountable 点出「清算」。

branches.en: TONE LINE: the word belongs to law and public office.
branches.cn: 语气线：这个词属于法律与公职。

intro.en: The account family with an ending that means able to be.
intro.cn: account 家族加一个表示「可被…」的词尾。

latinIntro.en: Computare, to reckon, became account, and -able made it a state someone can be put in.
latinIntro.cn: computare「计算」成为 account，-able 把它变成一种可以被置入的状态。

items.example: It marks what can be demanded.
items.exampleCN: 它标记可被要求的东西。

items.meaning: able to be called to account

items.meaningCN: 不受问责的、无法解释的

definition_zh: 会计工作；会计学；会计行业
definition_en: the work or the study of keeping and checking financial records
core_image: 一间办公室里，成排的账簿被逐页核对到最后一栏
scene: 她大学学的是会计，毕业后先进了一家小事务所。He teaches accountancy at a college in the north.
sceneCN: 这里 accountancy 是「会计学、会计工作」（第 1 个义项：记账查账的专业领域）；句意是他在北方一所学院教会计。

pos.zh: 名词：会计工作；会计学；会计行业

derivatives.zh: 义为「账目、报表」，常用复数

senses.title: The profession of keeping books
senses.titleCN: 会计工作：记账查账的职业
senses.definition: the work of keeping and auditing financial records
senses.definitionCN: 记录与核查财务记录的职业
senses.example: She trained in accountancy before joining the firm.
senses.exampleCN: 她进这家公司前受过会计训练。
senses.why: The -cy ending names a practice or a body of work, as in agency and currency.
senses.whyCN: -cy 词尾命名一种实务或一类工作，如 agency 与 currency。

senses.title: The academic subject
senses.titleCN: 会计学：作为学科的研究
senses.definition: the study of how financial records are made and checked
senses.definitionCN: 研究财务记录如何编制与核查的学科
senses.example: Accountancy is a required course in the programme.
senses.exampleCN: 会计学是这个项目的必修课。
senses.why: A practice taught in classrooms acquires a syllabus, and the noun covers the study too.
senses.whyCN: 成为课堂上传授的实务后有了教学大纲，这个名词也涵盖这门学问。

senses.title: The industry as a whole
senses.titleCN: 会计行业：由事务所构成的整体
senses.definition: the business of accounting firms and professionals
senses.definitionCN: 由会计师事务所与从业者构成的产业
senses.example: The accountancy sector hired more graduates this year.
senses.exampleCN: 会计行业今年招了更多毕业生。
senses.why: When the word takes a sector or a firm, it names the trade rather than the task.
senses.whyCN: 当这个词与行业或事务所搭配时，它命名的是行当，而非具体工作。

intro.en: Accountancy joins accountant, from the verb to account, with the Latin ending -ia through French -ie.
intro.cn: accountancy 由 accountant（源自动词 account）加拉丁词尾 -ia（经法语 -ie）构成。

items.en: Computare meant to reckon together, the root of all the account words.
items.cn: computare 意为「一同计算」，是所有 account 类词的词根。

items.en: Acont named a reckoning of money.
items.cn: acont 指对钱款的清算。

items.en: Accountant first meant answerable, then a keeper of accounts.
items.cn: accountant 先指「须交代的」，后指记账人。

items.en: Accountancy was coined as company law demanded records.
items.cn: 随着公司法要求账目记录，accountancy 被造出。

items.en: The word now names a profession and a degree subject.
items.cn: 这个词如今命名一个职业与一门学位课程。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the account family; the near-meaning group holds words for bookkeeping work.
note.cn: 形近组共用 account 家族；近义组收记账工作类词。

entries.definition: The person who practises accountancy.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「会计」，即从事此业的人。

entries.definition: The activity, especially in American use.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「会计」，美式更常用。

entries.definition: Answerable for what one does.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「负有责任的」。

entries.definition: The routine recording of daily entries.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「簿记」，偏日常记录。

entries.definition: The formal checking of accounts.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「审计」，偏核查。

entries.definition: The wider management of money.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「财务」，范围更宽。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the -ancy ending and the split between the trade and the subject.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借 -ancy 词尾，以及「行业」与「学科」的分工。

normal.en: Accountancy ends like agency and currency: a practice, not a person.
normal.cn: accountancy 的结尾像 agency 与 currency：它是一种实务，不是一个人。

normal.en: The accountant does accountancy, and accounting is the doing of it.
normal.cn: accountant 从事 accountancy，而 accounting 是那件做的事。

normal.en: British English prefers accountancy; American English leans on accounting.
normal.cn: 英式英语偏爱 accountancy，美式英语更常用 accounting。

normal.en: An accountancy firm sells nothing but accurate numbers.
normal.cn: 会计师事务所卖的东西只有一样：准确的数字。

normal.en: A degree in accountancy comes with a rule book thicker than the readings.
normal.cn: 会计学位附带的规则手册比阅读材料还厚。

abstract.en: A society invents a profession when it stops trusting memory with its money.
abstract.cn: 当一个社会不再把钱财托付给记忆时，它就发明一种职业。

abstract.en: Accountancy is arithmetic placed under oath.
abstract.cn: 会计学是被置于誓言之下的算术。

abstract.en: The -cy suffix turns a repeated act into an institution.
abstract.cn: -cy 词尾把反复的行为变成一个建制。

examples.en: He has a degree in accountancy from Leeds.
examples.cn: 他有一个利兹大学的会计学位。

examples.en: Accountancy rules changed again this year.
examples.cn: 会计规则今年又改了。

examples.en: She spent ten years in accountancy before teaching.
examples.cn: 她在教书前做了十年会计。

dict_mnemonic.text: accountant（会计）+ -cy（职业、状态）= 会计这一行

root: account（拉丁语 computare「计算」）+ -ant + -cy（表职业或状态）；同族词有 accountant、accounting、accountable。

sensesIntro.en: Accountancy names the craft, the classroom study of it, and the industry that sells it.
sensesIntro.cn: accountancy 命名这门手艺、对它的课堂研究，以及出售它的行业。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: rows of ledgers checked page by page.
core.cn: 核心意象：成排账簿被逐页核对。

branches.en: CRAFT LINE: the daily work of keeping books.
branches.cn: 手艺线：日常记账的工作。

branches.en: CLASSROOM LINE: the subject taught and examined.
branches.cn: 课堂线：被教授与考核的学科。

branches.en: MARKET LINE: firms and graduates form a sector.
branches.cn: 市场线：事务所与毕业生构成一个行业。

branches.en: CONTRAST: accountancy is the field, accounting the act.
branches.cn: 对照线：accountancy 是领域，accounting 是动作。

branches.en: TONE LINE: the word appears on degrees and in job ads.
branches.cn: 语气线：这个词出现在学位名与招聘广告里。

intro.en: The account family with endings that name a practice or a state.
intro.cn: account 家族加上命名实务或状态的词尾。

latinIntro.en: The Latin ending -ia, through French -ie, named a condition, and English -cy named a trade.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词尾 -ia 经法语 -ie 命名一种状态，英语的 -cy 则命名一个行当。

definition_en: a person whose job is to keep or check financial records
core_image: 一个人伏在桌前，一列数字顺着纸页直落到底
scene: 年底结账时，公司请来的会计师在会议室待了整整一周。She trained as an accountant before entering politics.
sceneCN: 这里 accountant 是「会计师」（第 1 个义项：以记账查账为职业的人）；句意是她在从政前受过会计师训练。

pos.zh: 名词：会计；会计师

senses.title: One who keeps the books
senses.titleCN: 会计：负责记账的人
senses.definition: a person who records money coming in and going out
senses.definitionCN: 记录钱款进出的人
senses.example: The accountant checks every invoice.
senses.exampleCN: 会计核对每一张发票。
senses.why: The -ant ending names the person who performs the act of accounting.
senses.whyCN: -ant 词尾指执行 account 这一行为的那个人。

senses.title: One who inspects the books
senses.titleCN: 查账者：负责审账的人
senses.definition: a person who examines records for accuracy
senses.definitionCN: 检查记录是否准确的人
senses.example: An outside accountant audited the firm.
senses.exampleCN: 一位外部会计师审计了这家公司。
senses.why: The same person may write the record or test it, and the title covers both.
senses.whyCN: 同一个人可以写记录，也可以检验记录，这个头衔两者都包括。

senses.title: A trained professional
senses.titleCN: 会计师：持证的专业人士
senses.definition: a qualified professional in accounting
senses.definitionCN: 会计领域的持证专业人员
senses.example: She is a chartered accountant in Leeds.
senses.exampleCN: 她是利兹的一名特许会计师。
senses.why: Modern licensing added a certificate to the older word, and a profession was named.
senses.whyCN: 现代的执照制度给这个旧词加上证书，一个职业由此得名。

intro.en: Accountant comes from French accountant, one who accounts, built on the verb accontier, to reckon.
intro.cn: accountant 来自法语 accountant「记账者」，构于动词 accontier「清算」之上。

items.en: Computare meant to reckon together, the root behind account.
items.cn: computare 意为「一同计算」，是 account 背后的词根。

items.en: Acont named a reckoning of money.
items.cn: acont 指对钱款的清算。

items.en: French used accountant for a person who renders accounts.
items.cn: 法语用 accountant 指交代账目的人。

items.en: English accountant first meant answerable, then a keeper of accounts.
items.cn: 英语 accountant 起初指「须交代的」，后指记账人。

items.en: Chartered and certified bodies turned the word into a profession.
items.cn: 特许与注册机构把这个词变成一个职业。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the account family; the near-meaning group holds finance jobs.
note.cn: 形近组共用 account 家族；近义组收财务职业类词。

entries.definition: A record of money or a report.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「账户、账目」。

entries.definition: The profession or study of accounting.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「会计工作、会计学」。

entries.definition: Required to answer for what one does.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「负有责任的」。

entries.definition: One who records daily entries, often less qualified.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「记账员」，资历通常较浅。

entries.definition: One who formally inspects accounts.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「审计员」，偏检查。

entries.definition: One who holds and manages a group's money.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「财务主管」，偏管钱。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the -ant person ending and the difference from bookkeeper.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借 -ant 表人的词尾，以及与 bookkeeper 的区别。

normal.en: Add -ant to account and you get the person who does the accounting.
normal.cn: account 后加 -ant，就得到做账的那个人。

normal.en: An accountant turns a year of receipts into one page of figures.
normal.cn: 会计师把一整年的票据变成一页数字。

normal.en: Accountant ends in -ant like servant and assistant, all people.
normal.cn: accountant 以 -ant 结尾，和 servant、assistant 一样，都是人。

normal.en: Accountancy is the trade, accounting the activity, accountant the worker.
normal.cn: accountancy 是行业，accounting 是活动，accountant 是从业者。

normal.en: A bookkeeper records; an accountant judges and signs.
normal.cn: bookkeeper 记录，accountant 判断并签字。

abstract.en: The accountant is the person a society hires to remember its numbers honestly.
abstract.cn: 会计师是一个社会雇来诚实地记住它那些数字的人。

abstract.en: Trust is the real material: the figures on the page only work if someone signs them.
abstract.cn: 真正的材料是信任：纸上的数字只有在有人签字后才算数。

abstract.en: Every profession leaves a suffix behind that tells you who is standing there.
abstract.cn: 每个职业都留下一个词尾，告诉你站在那里的那个人是谁。

examples.en: Our accountant handles all the tax papers.
examples.cn: 我们的会计处理所有的税务文件。

examples.en: She became an accountant after ten years in sales.
examples.cn: 她做了十年销售后成了会计师。

examples.en: The accountant found two errors in the books.
examples.cn: 会计在账目里发现了两处错误。

dict_mnemonic.text: account（账目）+ -ant（…的人）= 管账目的人 → 会计

root: account（拉丁语 computare「计算」经法语）+ -ant（表人的词尾）；同族词有 accountancy、accounting、accountable。

sensesIntro.en: Accountant names the person first, and the certificate comes later, so the word holds both the worker and the profession.
sensesIntro.cn: accountant 先命名人，证书是后来的事，因此这个词既装下干活的人，也装下一个职业。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a figure bent over a long column of numbers.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人伏在长长一列数字前。

branches.en: RECORD LINE: money in and out is written down.
branches.cn: 记录线：钱的进出被写下。

branches.en: CHECK LINE: the records are tested for error.
branches.cn: 检查线：记录被查错。

branches.en: PROFESSION LINE: a licence names the trade.
branches.cn: 职业线：执照给行业命名。

branches.en: CONTRAST: a bookkeeper enters, an accountant signs.
branches.cn: 对照线：bookkeeper 入账，accountant 签字。

branches.en: TRUST LINE: the signature is what the public buys.
branches.cn: 信任线：公众买的正是那个签名。

intro.en: The account family with the Latin ending that names the person doing the act.
intro.cn: account 家族加上一个命名「做此事之人」的拉丁词尾。

latinIntro.en: Accounts were kept by a computator in Latin, and French called the same man accountant.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语里记账的人叫 computator，法语把同一个人叫 accountant。
